## 20.4. Bahuvrīhi with casus obliquus first member

i.e. Bahuvrīhi, whose first member represents a case other than the nominative (⟪प्रथमा⟫).

Example:

::: indent
⟪देवरूपा⟫ = ⟪देवस्यैव⟫ ⟪रूपं⟫ ⟪यस्याः⟫ ⟪सा⟫ = "a (woman), whose form is that of a god" "a woman of divine appearance"
:::
::: grammar-box

**Exception to the general rule regarding the order of compound members:**

**The casus obliquus member stands in the second position if it denotes a body part (esp. the hand):**

**Example:**

:::
::: indent
⟪दण्डहस्तः⟫ =  ⟪दण्डो⟫ ⟪हस्ते⟫ (Loc. sg.) ⟪यस्य⟫ ⟪सः⟫ = "one, in whose hand a staff is located" = "one who carries a staff in his hand."
:::
::: media
![](/images/lekt2001.webp)
Fig.: ⟪इन्द्रो⟫ ⟪वज्रपाणिः⟫
Siemreap (ក្រុងសៀមរាប), Cambodia, 9th cent. CE
(Image source: [Details](/en/licenses#lekt2001))
:::
## 20.5. Bahuvrīhi with adverbial first member

The first member contains an adverb, a preposition, a preverb, or another indeclinable; such compounds are generally ⟪नित्यसमास⟫.

Examples:

::: indent
⟪अपुत्रो⟫ ⟪नरः⟫ = ⟪पुत्रो⟫ ⟪यस्य⟫ ⟪नास्ति⟫ ⟪स⟫ ⟪नरः⟫ = "a man who has no son" = "a sonless man"

⟪दुर्बल⟫ ⟪३⟫ = "someone / something whose strength is bad" = "weak, feeble"
:::
::: grammar-box

**⟪सह⟫ "with" as the first member of a Bahuvrīhi is often replaced by ⟪स⟫.**

**Example:**
27b337176bb7b57fe956573bada382cb:
:::
::: indent
⟪सपुत्रः⟫ =  ⟪सहपुत्रः⟫ =  ⟪पुत्रेण⟫ ⟪सहितः⟫ ⟪।⟫ ⟪पुत्रेण⟫ ⟪सह्⟫ = "with a son", "accompanied by a son"
:::
::: media
![](/images/lekt2006.webp)

Madhya Pradesh
(Image source: [Details](/en/licenses#lekt2006))

## 20.6. Inflection of the final member of a Bahuvrīhi

::: grammar-box

**The final member of a Bahuvrīhi is inflected as a multi-gender adjective, regardless of its original gender. Thus, if in a compound the final member has a gender different from its original one, it must be a Bahuvrīhi, unless it is a Samāhāradvanva (Neuter singular).**

**In adjectivization,**

*   **-ā-stems in Masculine and Neuter become -a-stems**
*   **-a-stems (m., n.) form their Feminine on -ā or -ī**
*   **-ī-stems (f.) must take the suffix -ka, -kā, -ka (n.) at the end of Bahuvrīhis; this suffix can or must also be taken by many other Bahuvrīhis**

:::
## 20.7. Another classification of types of Bahuvrīhis

The examples here are given for later study; for some, the necessary grammar and vocabulary have not yet been discussed.

1.  qualifying word in the first member -- qualified word in the second member: ⟪स्थिरचित्तः⟫ = ⟪स्थिरं⟫ ⟪चित्तं⟫ ⟪यस्य⟫ ⟪सः⟫
2.  indeclinables in the first member: ⟪उच्चैःश्रवस्⟫
3.  comparison in the first member: ⟪कुशाग्रधीः⟫ =  ⟪कुशाग्र⟫ ⟪इव⟫ ⟪धीर्यस्य⟫ ⟪सः⟫
4.  implicit comparison: ⟪उष्ट्रमुखः⟫ = ⟪उष्ट्रस्य⟫ ⟪मुखमिव⟫ ⟪मुखं⟫ ⟪यस्य⟫ ⟪सः⟫ = "camel-mouthed" = whose mouth is like that of a camel
5.  numeral as the second member for approximate number: ⟪उपसशाः⟫ = ⟪दशानां⟫ ⟪समीपे⟫ ⟪ये⟫ ⟪सन्ति⟫ ⟪ते⟫ = "approximately ten"
6.  both members are numerals: ⟪एकद्वाः⟫ = ⟪एको⟫ ⟪वा⟫ ⟪द्वौ⟫ ⟪वा⟫ = "one or two"
7.  with sa-/saha- in the first member: ⟪सपुत्रः⟫ ⟪।⟫ ⟪सहपुत्रः⟫
8.  with sa- (= ⟪समान⟫) in the first member: ⟪सजनपदः⟫ = ⟪समानो⟫ ⟪जनपदो⟫ ⟪यस्य⟫ ⟪सः⟫
9.  ⟪नञ्बहुव्रीहिः⟫ = with a-/an- in the first member: ⟪अपुत्रः⟫ = ⟪न⟫ ⟪विद्यते⟫ ⟪पुत्रो⟫ ⟪यस्य⟫ ⟪सः⟫ ; ⟪अनङ्गः⟫ = ⟪न⟫ ⟪विद्यते⟫ ⟪अङ्गं⟫ ⟪यस्य⟫ ⟪सः⟫

## 20.8. Relationship between Bahuvrīhi and Relative Clause

Although every Bahuvrīhi can be resolved into a relative clause, not every relative clause can be replaced by a Bahuvrīhi. Hermann Georg Jacobi (1850 - 1937), who examined the relationship between the two in more detail (Compositum und Nebensatz, 1897), writes:

::: indent
"If one translates from German or another modern language into Sanskrit, not all subordinate clauses can be rendered by compounds, but only the embellishing and descriptive ones; those, however, which contain a conceptually necessary or important determination, also appear in Sanskrit as relative clauses."
2af57b6f596df3efcf63760c31753a04:
:::
::: media
![](/images/lekt2002.jpg)
Fig.: Hermann Jacobi
(Image source: [Details](/en/licenses#lekt2002))
:::
That may be true. However, then the Indians view many things as embellishing and descriptive, which we would consider "conceptually necessary or important."

# Lesson 14

## 14.1. The Expression of the Relationship of Noun-Designated Entities: the Genitive (ṣaṣṭhī f. = ⟪षष्टी⟫ = sixth case ending)

::: grammar-box
If the relationship expressed by two nouns is to be indicated, the genitive (ṣaṣṭhī f. "sixth case ending") is used. The genitive differs from all other cases in that it -- with a few exceptions -- does not serve to further specify the action expressed by the verb, but rather to express the relationship between persons or things designated by nouns. Frequently, the genitive answers the question: Whose?
:::
Examples:

⟪कवेः⟫ ⟪पुत्रः⟫ "The poet's son"

⟪धनस्य⟫ ⟪लोभः⟫ "Greed for wealth"

⟪नगरस्यार्धम्⟫ "The half of the city"

⟪रामस्य⟫ ⟪कृतम्⟫ "The / A deed of Rāma"

::: grammar-box
The normal word order is:

> **Determining word in the genitive — Further specified noun in another case**
:::
**Genitive and PPP:**

::: grammar-box
With PPPs, the genitive can stand instead of the instrumental (tṛtīyā) for the agent (kartṛ); In the construction with the instrumental, the PPP is regarded as a passive verbal form (that which stands in the instrumental denotes the agent), in the construction with the genitive, the PPP is regarded as a noun or adjective (that which stands in the genitive is thus not actually an agent).

According to Pāṇini 2.3.67, with a PPP in the genitive, if the PPP has present-tense meaning (see above), the instrumental is used if the PPP has past-tense meaning:

> ⟪रामस्येष्टं⟫ ⟪फलम्⟫ "The fruit desired by Rāma = The fruit that Rāma currently desires"
> 
> ⟪रामेणेष्टं⟫ ⟪फलम्⟫ "The fruit that Rāma has desired"

Naturally, with a neuter singular PPP used as a verbal abstract -- i.e., as a noun -- the genitive is used.
:::
## 14.2. Formation of Genitive Forms (ṣaṣṭhī f. = ⟪षष्ठी⟫)

The genitive is formed from the weak stem for verbal stems with stem gradation.

**Genitive of consonant-ending stems:**

::: grammar-box

After a consonant, the regular genitive endings are:
* Singular: **-as**
* Plural: **-ām**

:::
::: center

| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |

| **paśu-mant-** :br ⟪पशुमन्त्⟫ | **paśu-mat-** :br ⟪पशुमत्⟫ | **paśu-mat-as** :br ⟪पशुमतस्⟫ | **paśu-mat-ām** :br ⟪पशुमताम्⟫ |

:::

**Formal identity:**

::: important

In all nominal stems except for masculines and neuters ending in -a, and except for pronouns, the form of the genitive singular is identical to that of the ablative (pañcamī "fifth case ending") singular!

Note that in consonant-final stems, the ablative and genitive singular sound the same as the accusative plural masculine and feminine!

:::
## 14.3. Further on the use of the genitive (⟪षष्ठी⟫)

::: grammar-box
Contrary to the basic rule above, the genitive is used to express the object of certain verbs, e.g. verbs of remembrance:

> ⟪देवानां⟫ ⟪स्मरति⟫ "He remembers the gods"

With all these verbs, however, the object can also be in the accusative:

> ⟪देवान्स्मरति⟫ "He remembers the gods"

More on this later.
:::

**Translation:**
Ten fools. The antics of fools are mostly entertaining. For example: Once, ten fools set out to wander around the country. After they had gone a short distance, a deep river blocked their path. Rowing with their arms, they somehow crossed the river and reached the other bank.

Among them was an elder. He wanted to know if everyone had reached the bank, so he counted each one individually. But he counted only nine. Then he shouted: "Hey! We set out as ten, now we are only nine! Surely one has drowned in the river! Search for him!" Thereupon, each one of them counted individually. But there were always only nine! Then they became agitated, and a great uproar ensued. Not far from there was the hermitage of a Ṛṣi. The sage dwelling there observed their behavior and laughed aloud. The fools heard his laughter, rushed to him, and asked for the reason. The Ṛṣi said: "Ha! You do not know yourselves. Each of you failed to count himself. That is why this confusion arose." When they heard this, the fools departed, ashamed and with bowed heads.

## 51.1. ⟪उपपद⟫-Compounds

::: grammar-box
**⟪उपपद⟫-Compounds (⟪उपपद⟩ n. "accompanying word") are ⟪तत्पुरुष⟩ with a verbal noun as the second member, which occurs only as the second member of compounds, but not as an independent, single word. ⟪उपपद⟩ are formed with the ⟪कृत्⟩ suffixes**
* **-Ø**
* **-a**
* **-t**

**They are nomina agentis, i.e., they designate an agent (⟪कर्तृ⟩), who performs the action designated by the underlying root.**

**Such compounds are not resolved by native commentators through nominal combinations, but rather by means of verbal forms:**

Examples:

:::
::: indent
⟪सुखकरः⟫ = ⟪सुखं⟫ ⟪करोतीति⟫ ⟪सुखकरः⟫

## 51.2. Declension of stems ending in a simple consonant (except nasal, semivowel, -s)

::: grammar-box
**Stems ending in a simple consonant (except nasal, semivowel, -s) have no stem gradation. The declension occurs completely regularly by attaching the regular case endings.**

**Singular irregularity: in the Nom., Acc., Voc. pl. Neut., a nasal is inserted before the stem ending.**
:::
### 51.2.1. Stems ending in a non-palatal stop
caf0f3d8dd8e9bd96076427ba7cd4a98:
::: grammar-box
**The usual sound change laws apply, i.e.**
* **in final position, the corresponding voiceless non-aspirate stands**
* **before the -su of the Loc. pl., the final position is first replaced by the corresponding voiceless non-aspirate, then the corresponding sound changes occur**
* **before a voiced consonant, the final position is replaced by the corresponding voiced non-aspirate.**
:::
Examples:

⟪शत्रुजित्⟫ 3 "conquering enemies"

::: indent
Masculine, Feminine:

:::
::: indent
Singular:

:::
::: indent
Nom.Voc. ⟪शत्रुजित्⟫ (śatrujit + s)
Acc. ⟪शत्रुजितम्⟫
:::
Plural:

::: indent
Nom.Acc.Voc. ⟪शत्रुजितस्⟫
Instr. ⟪शत्रुजिद्भिस्⟫
Loc. ⟪शत्रुजित्सु⟫
:::

::: indent

:::

Singular.Nom.Voc.m.f.n. ⟪सुयुत्⟫
etc.
:::
Complete paradigms in Kielhorn, Grammar pp. 16ff.

### 51.2.2. Stems ending in a palatal stop (c, ch, j), ś, ṣ

::: grammar-box
**Before a vowel-initial ending, the stem final remains unchanged.**

**Before the other endings:**

* **final -c and -j are replaced by k, and the stem is then treated as if it ended in -k**
* **in some words (list in Kielhorn, Grammar p. 18), final -j is replaced by -ṭ**
* **final -ch is replaced by -ṭ**
* **final -ś and -ṣ are replaced by -ṭ, with some exceptions. In the exceptional cases, -ś and -ṣ are replaced by -k**

**i.e.**

* **-c » -k**
* **-ch » -ṭ**
* **-j » -k or -ṭ**

### 51.2.3. Stems ending in -h

::: grammar-box
**Before a vowel-initial ending, the -h remains unchanged.**

**Before the other endings**
* **usually the -h is replaced by -ḍh**
* **if the underlying root begins with d-, the -h is replaced by -gh. Similarly, in some other words, optionally or obligatorily (compilation in Kielhorn, Grammar §80,2)**
* **(in the final position of the root noun, -h is replaced by -dh)**

**After these substitutions, the stem is treated further as if it ended in -ḍh, -gh, or -dh.**

::: note-box
Regarding ⟪ऋतु⟫ see Manu III, 45-48: according to this, ⟪ऋतु⟫ lasts 16 days (according to the alternative translation: 20 days) from the start of menstruation, sexual intercourse is forbidden on the first four days after the start of bleeding (according to the alternative translation: on the first eight (4 + 4) days), as well as on the 11th (or 15th) and 13th (or 18th) day. On even days, the woman conceives sons; on odd days, daughters. For the following, a ⟪ऋतु⟫ of a total of 16 days (not the alternative translation) is assumed, as most indigenous commentaries do, and which was therefore the prevailing view.

Since ovulation occurs 14 days before the start of menstruation, with this determination of the fertile period, fertility is almost "guaranteed" for a menstrual cycle interval of 19 to 30 days. The forbidden days (11th and 13th) improve the probability of sexual intercourse on the 12th and 14th days, i.e., the probability of conception in a 28-day cycle (the lifespan of sperm in the woman is approx. 3 days). These regulations are as it were a positive application of the Knaus-Ogino method.

### 41.2.1. लट्-शत्रुप्रत्ययः आत्मनेपदम्, लट्-कर्मणि शत्रुप्रत्ययः, लृट्-शत्रुप्रत्ययः आत्मनेपदम्

#### 41.2.1.1. Thematic present stems, passive and future

::: grammar-box
**Formation:**

Present stem / passive stem / future stem + -māna (fem. mānā)
:::
Examples:

⟪यज्⟫ 1U, Pres.Part.Ā ⟪यजमान⟫ 3 "one who is honored with a sacrifice for one's own benefit = sacrificer"

⟪मन्⟫ 4Ā, Pres.Part.Ā  ⟪मन्यमान⟫ 3 "a thinker"

⟪कृ⟫ 8U, Pres.Part.Passive ⟪क्रियमाण⟫ 3 "something that is done"

⟪दा⟫ 3U, Fut.Part.Ā ⟪दास्यमान⟫ 3 "one who will give for one's own benefit"

#### 41.2.1.2. A-thematic present classes

::: grammar-box
**Formation:**

Weak present stem (in the form it has before the ending -ate of the 3.pl.Ā) + -āna (fem. -ānā)
:::
Examples:

::: grammar-box
| Root / Klasse | Partizip Present Ā |
| :--- | :--- |
| **⟪द्विष्⟫** 2U | ⟪द्विषाण⟫ |
| **⟪हु⟫** 3P | \<⟪जुह्वान⟫\>:brju-hu + āna |
| **⟪सु⟫** 5U | ⟪सुन्वान⟫:brsu-nu + āna |
| **⟪रुध्⟫** 7U | ⟪रुन्धान⟫:brru-n-dh-āna |
| **⟪तन्⟫** 8U | ⟪तन्वान⟫:brtan-u + āna |
| **⟪क्री⟫** 9U | ⟪क्रीणान⟫:brkrī + n-āna |
:::
### 41.2.2. "Participle" of passive necessity (Gerundive) (⟪कृत्य⟫)

::: grammar-box
**To express passive necessity ("what must/should be done"), adjectives derived from roots and derived verbal stems can optionally be formed with the following suffixes:**

* **-⟪तव्य⟫** (fem. **-⟪तव्या⟫**)
* **-⟪अनीय⟫** (fem. **-⟪अनीया⟫**)
* **-⟪य⟫** (fem. **-⟪या⟫**)
* **-⟪त्य⟫** (fem. **-⟪त्या⟫**) (instead of **-⟪य⟫**/**-⟪या⟫**)
:::
#### 41.2.2.1. The suffix -⟪तव्य⟫ / -⟪तव्या⟫

::: grammar-box
**The suffix -⟪तव्य⟫ / -⟪तव्या⟫ is attached to roots and derived verbal stems (e.g. causative) in the same way as the infinitive suffix -⟪तुम्⟫ (see [Lesson 23](lektion23.md)), i.e.**

* **guṇa-grade root + ⟪तव्य⟫**

or

* **guṇa-grade root + -i- + ⟪तव्य⟫**

**In the causative:**

* **causative stem on -ay + -i- + ⟪तव्य⟫**
:::
Examples:

::: no-header

| | | |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| ⟪जि⟫ 1P | ⟪जेतव्य⟫ 3 | "one who must be conquered; one to be conquered" |
| ⟪वृत्⟫ 1Ā | ⟪वर्तितव्य⟫ 3 | "that where one should be located" |
| ⟪बुध्⟫ Caus. | ⟪बोधयितव्य⟫ | "one who should be awakened; one to be awakened" |

:::
#### 41.2.2.2. The suffix -⟪अनीय⟫ / -⟪अनीया⟫

::: grammar-box
**Formation:**

High-grade root + -⟪अनीय⟫ / -⟪अनीया⟫

**Causative and 10th Present Class:**

Root, as it appears in the causative stem, without -aya- + -⟪अनीय⟫ / -⟪अनीया⟫
:::
Examples:

::: no-header

| | | |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| ⟪दा⟫ 3U | ⟪दानीय⟫ 3 | "to be given; what must be given" |
| ⟪जि⟫ 1P | ⟪जयनीय⟫ 3 | "to be conquered" |
| ⟪कृ⟫ 8U | ⟪करणीय⟫ 3 | "to be done" |
| ⟪दृश्⟫ | ⟪दर्शनीय⟫ 3 | "what must be seen; worth seeing" |
| ⟪बुध्⟫ Caus. | ⟪बोधनीय⟫ 3:brbodh-aya - aya + -anīya | "one to be awakened" |
| ⟪दा⟫ Caus. | ⟪दापनीय⟫ 3:brdā-paya - aya + -anīya | "what must be caused to be given" |

:::
#### 41.2.2.3. The Suffix -⟪य⟫ / -⟪या⟫

::: grammar-box
**Formation:**

Root (in low, high, or guṇa grade) + -⟪य⟫

For the exact rules, see Kielhorn, Grammar of the Sanskrit Language, pp. 195 - 197!
:::
Treatment of final vowels:

::: grammar-box
**1. Roots ending in -ā form this gerundive in -eya**
:::
Examples:

::: no-header

| | | |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| ⟪ज्ञा⟫ 9U | ⟪ज्ञेय⟫ 3 | "to be known; what must be recognized" |
| ⟪दा⟫ 3U | ⟪देय⟫ 3 | "what must be given" |

:::
::: grammar-box
**2. Roots ending in -i /-ī / -u / -ū /-ṛ generally have high or guṇa grade, unless they belong to those roots ending in -i / -u /-ṛ that form a gerundive with the suffix -⟪त्य⟫ (fem. -⟪त्या⟫) (list of these roots in Kielhorn, Grammar §537).**
:::
Example:

::: no-header

| | | |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| ⟪स्मृ⟫ 1P | ⟪स्मर्य⟫ 3 | "that which must be remembered" |

:::
::: grammar-box
**2a. Roots ending in -i/-ī have high grade**
:::
Examples:

::: no-header

| | | |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| ⟪विक्री⟫ 9Ā | ⟪विक्रेय⟫ 3 | "to be sold; saleable" |
| ⟪नी⟫ 1U | ⟪नेय⟫ 3 | "to be led" |

:::

::: grammar-box
**2b. Roots ending in -u /-ū replace the high-grade -o before -ya with -av, and the guṇa-grade -au with -āv. Guṇa-grade formation in this case denotes necessity.**
:::
Example:

| :--- | :--- | :--- |

|   | ⟪स्ताव्य⟫ 3 | "that which must necessarily be praised" |

:::

#### 41.2.2.4. The suffix -⟪त्य⟫ / ⟪त्या⟫ (instead of -⟪य⟫ / -⟪या⟫)

::: grammar-box
List of roots ending in -i / -u /-ṛ, which form a gerundive not with -⟪य⟫ / -⟪या⟫ but with the suffix -⟪त्य⟫ (fem. -⟪त्या⟫), in Kielhorn, Grammar §537.

:::
### 41.2.3. Syntactic usage of the "participle" of passive necessity (Gerundivum) (⟪कृत्य⟫)

::: grammar-box
The gerundive can be used attributively:

:::
::: indent
**⟪दर्शनीयं⟫ ⟪नगरम्⟫** = "a city that must be seen; a city worth seeing"
:::
The gerundive can also be used as a predicative noun in sentences with a passive construction expressing an obligation or command (with ⟪न⟫ a prohibition, an impossibility):

::: indent
**⟪काशी⟫ ⟪द्विजैर्द्रष्टव्या⟫** = "Twice-born must see Benares"
:::
::: media
![lekt4108.jpg](/images/lekt4108.webp)
Fig.: ⟪दर्शनीयं⟫ ⟪नगरं⟫ ⟪काशी⟫
(Image source: [Details](/en/licenses#lekt4108))
:::
### 41.2.4. Differences in the usage of the gerundive suffixes

::: grammar-box
The usage of these suffixes largely overlaps

* **-⟪तव्य⟫ (fem. -⟪तव्या⟫):** always expresses necessity and is preferably used predicatively (less frequently attributively). Formations with this suffix should not be used in nominal compounds.
* **-⟪अनीय⟫ (fem. -⟪अनीया⟫) and -⟪य⟫ (fem. -⟪या⟫) / -⟪त्य⟫ (fem. -⟪त्या⟫) (instead of -⟪य⟫/-⟪या⟫):** can have an additional meaning (esp. -⟪य⟫) in the sense of the German "-worthy" (e.g. "worth seeing") or only a possibility "-able" (⟪दृश्य⟫ "visible"). Formations with these suffixes can be negated with ⟪अ⟫-/-⟪अन्⟫- (but not formations with -⟪तव्य⟫) and there are ⟪तत्पुरुष⟫ as their second member in which they occur.
:::
### 41.2.5. No connection with ⟪सु⟫- and ⟪दुस्⟫-

::: grammar-box
With  ⟪सु⟫- and ⟪दुस्⟫- in the meaning "easy" or "difficult", gerundives must not be connected. Instead, ⟪तत्पुरुष⟫ of the type  ⟪सुकर⟫ 3 ("easy to do") are used (see [Lesson 18](lektion18.md)).
:::

**In this lesson you will learn:**

- Vocabulary related to sacrifice, truth, and social roles
:::
## 10.1. The Passive Sentence

::: grammar-box
**Schema:**
**(Agent - kartṛ - in the Instrumental (tṛtīyā)) - (direct object - karman - in the Nominative) - passive verbal form**

e.g. **brāhmaṇena deva ijyate** = ⟪ब्राह्मणेन⟫ ⟪देव⟫ ⟪इज्यते⟫ = "A Brahman worships a god with a sacrifice" (literally: "A god is worshipped by a Brahman with a sacrifice.")

This sentence is **completely (!) semantically identical** to the sentence:
**brāhmaṇo devaṃ yajati / yajate** = ⟪ब्राह्मणो⟫ ⟪देवं⟫ ⟪यजति⟫ / ⟪यजते⟫
:::

::: grammar-box
- In the passive sentence, the agent (**kartṛ**) stands in the **Instrumental** (tṛtīyā f. "third case ending"), and the direct object (**karman** n.) stands in the **Nominative** (prathamā f.).
- Passive sentences in which the agent is not specified usually have an impersonal meaning ("one"):
  e.g. **ijyate** = ⟪इज्यते⟫ "One sacrifices" (literally: "it is worshipped with a sacrifice").
:::

::: grammar-box
**Even if the corresponding active sentence contained an accusative (dvitīyā) of the goal, this can be put into the Nominative (prathamā) in the passive sentence:**

The active sentence **rāmo grāmaṃ gacchati** = ⟪रामो⟫ ⟪ग्रामं⟫ ⟪गच्छति⟫ = "Rāma goes to the village." corresponds to the passive sentences:
- **rāmeṇa grāmaṃ gamyate** = ⟪रामेण⟫ ⟪ग्रामं⟫ ⟪गम्यते⟫
- alternatively: **rāmeṇa grāmo gamyate** = ⟪रामेण⟫ ⟪ग्रामो⟫ ⟪गम्यते⟫
:::

::: grammar-box
**Intransitive verbs (verbs without a direct object) frequently have passive constructions, especially in polite requests:**
- **praviśyatām** = ⟪प्रविश्यताम्⟫ = "One may enter = Please enter = Come in!"
- **niṣadyatām** = ⟪निषद्यताम्⟫ = "One may sit down = Please sit down = Please take a seat"
:::
Sanskrit passive constructions are extremely frequent: the passive is, after all, easier to form than, for example, numerous present stems.

::: important
**Sanskrit passive sentences generally must not be rendered in German by a passive sentence, since the German passive has a completely different stylistic function.**
:::

### 10.2.1. On the Usage of the Instrumental (tṛtīyā = ⟪तृतीया⟫)

::: grammar-box
**The Instrumental (tṛtīyā) primarily answers the questions:**
- **By what?**
- **With what?**
- **With whom?**

**It stands**
1. **in passive sentences: Agent (kartṛ) in the Instrumental**
2. **to indicate the means or instrument with which something is accomplished**
3. **to indicate the path by which someone reaches somewhere**
4. **to express connection, union, accompaniment with**
5. **with postpositions meaning "together with, with"; e.g. saha = ⟪सह⟫ = "with"** :brz.B.:br **brāhmaṇena saha** = ⟪ब्राह्मणेन⟫ ⟪सह⟫ = "together with the Brahmin"
:::
Further uses of the Instrumental (tṛtīyā) follow later.

## 10.3. The so-called Cerebralization Law for -n- (a word sandhi)

::: grammar-box
An **-n-**, followed by a vowel or **n, m, y, v**, is replaced by **-ṇ-** if **ṛ, ṝ, r, ṣ** precede the **-n-** in the word or if no other sound than vowels, Gutturals, Labials, **y, v, h** or Anusvāra stands between these sounds and the following **-n-** in the word.
:::
**Therefore:**

| | Instrumental Singular |
| :--- | :--- |
| **guru** :br⟪गुरु⟫ | **guruṇā** :br⟪गुरुणा⟫ |
| **śūdra** :br⟪शूद्र⟫ | **śūdreṇa** :br⟪शूद्रेण⟫ |

## 10.4. The Passive, Indicative Present (yak = ⟪यक्⟫)

::: grammar-box
**Formation:**
**(mostly) guṇa-grade root + -ya- + Ātmanepada ending**
:::
e.g.

| Root:br⟪धातु⟫ | 3. sg. Pass. Präs. Indik.:br⟪यक्⟫ ⟪लट्⟫ | 3. pl. Pass. Präs. Indik.:br⟪यक्⟫ ⟪लट्⟫ |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **nī** :br1 U:br(nayati) | **nīyate** :br(⟪नीयते⟫):br"er wird geführt" | **nīyante** :br(⟪नीयन्ते⟫) |
| **man** :br4 Ā:br(manyate) | **manyate** :br(⟪मन्यते⟫):br"er wird gedacht" | **manyante** :br(⟪मन्यन्ते⟫) |
| **viś** :br6 P:br(viśati) | **viśyate** :br(⟪विश्यते⟫):br"es wird betreten" | **viśyante** :br(⟪विश्यन्ते⟫) |

**Note that for verbs of the 4th present class, the Ātmanepada and the passive have identical forms! Whether Ātmanepada or passive is present can only be inferred from the sentence construction in this case.**

### 10.4.1. Special rules for the formation of the passive

1. **Roots ending in -i or -u** lengthen their vowel before the passive suffix **-ya-**:
   * **ji** 1 P: **jīyate**, **jīyante** :br⟪जीयते⟫, ⟪जीयन्ते⟫
   * **śru** 5 P: **śrūyate**, **śrūyante** :br⟪श्रूयते⟫, ⟪श्रूयन्ते⟫
   * **su** 5 U: **sūyate**, **sūyante** :br⟪सूयते⟫, ⟪सूयन्ते⟫

2. **Roots with -a- between consonants** (except nasals, y, r, v) remain in guṇa-grade:
   * **labh** 1 Ā: **labhyate**, **labhyante** :br⟪लभ्यते⟫, ⟪लभ्यन्ते⟫

3. **Some roots form their passive in guṇa-grade** (or in the ablaut grade of the present stem):
   * **āp** 5 P: **āpyate**, **āpyante** :br⟪आप्यते⟫, ⟪आप्यन्ते⟫
   * **khād** 1 P: **khādyate**, **khādyante** :br⟪खाद्यते⟫, ⟪खाद्यन्ते⟫
   * **smṛ** 1 P: **smaryate**, **smaryante** :br⟪स्मर्यते⟫, ⟪स्मर्यन्ते⟫

4. **Low-grade of verbs beginning with ya, va, ra, or where these sounds stand after another consonant (Samprasāraṇa = ⟪सम्प्रसारण⟫):**

   | Root:br⟪धातु⟫ | Tiefstufe:br⟪सम्प्रसारण⟫ | Passiv:br⟪यक्⟫ |
   | :--- | :--- | :--- |
   | **yaj** 1 U:br⟪यज्⟫ | \*yj » ij | **ijyate** :br⟪इज्यते⟫:br **ijyante** :br⟪इज्यन्ते⟫ |
   | **vad** 1 P:br⟪वद्⟫ | \*vd » ud | **udyate** :br⟪उद्यते⟫:br **udyante** :br⟪उद्यन्ते⟫ |
   | **prach** 6 P:br⟪प्रच्छ्⟫ | \*prcch » pṛcch | **pṛcchyate** :br⟪पृच्छ्यते⟫:br **pṛcchyante** :br⟪पृच्छ्यन्ते⟫ |

Der traditionelle indigene Name für diese untergeordnete Bildung in Verben mit **ya** oder **va** ist **Samprasāraṇa** (⟪नपुंसकम्⟫ = ⟪सम्प्रसारण⟫).

5. **Final -ṛ** after a single consonant is replaced by **-ri-** before the passive suffix **-ya-**:
   * **kṛ** 8 U: **kriyate**, **kriyante** :br⟪क्रियते⟫, ⟪क्रियन्ते⟫
   * But: **smṛ** 1 P: **smaryate** :br⟪स्मर्यते⟫

6. **Some roots ending in -an have alternatively two passive stem formations:**
   * an **-an-ya**
   * an **-ā-ya-** (the long **ā** is a representative of a hypothetical long nasal)
230d6b1481ebdf4f5486d1ce7828a7f9:
e.g. **tan** 8 U.
   * **tan-ya-te**, **tan-ya-nte** :br⟪तन्यते⟫, ⟪तन्यन्ते⟫
   * **tā-ya-te**, **tā-ya-nte** :br⟪तायते⟫, ⟪तायन्ते⟫ (from \*tn-ya-nte)

## 24.1. The Dative (⟪चतुर्थी⟫ = "fourth case ending")

::: grammar-box
**1. To express the purpose or intention ("in order to") of an action, instead of the infinitive (⟪तुमुन्⟫), one can also use a noun with a kṛt suffix, which denotes an action or state, in the dative (⟪चतुर्थी⟫ = "fourth case ending").**

Example:

instead of:

:::
::: indent
⟪रामो⟫ ⟪गुरुवचनं⟫ ⟪श्रोतुं⟫ ⟪गतः⟫ ⟪।⟫
:::
one can also say:

::: indent
⟪रामो⟫ ⟪गुरुवचनस्य⟫ ⟪श्रवणाय⟫ ⟪गतः⟫ ⟪।⟫

or:

⟪रामो⟫ ⟪गुरुवचनश्रवणाय⟫ ⟪गतः⟫ ⟪।⟫
:::
= "Rāma has gone to hear the teacher's speech."

::: grammar-box
**2. The dative (⟪चतुर्थी⟫) can also denote the object of an infinitive of purpose to be supplied:**

Example:

:::
**In the same way, the dative (⟪चतुर्थी⟫) denotes the purpose of a thing or an action:**

Example:

## 24.3. Sandhi of final -ai and -au

::: grammar-box
**Sandhi of final -ai and -au**

* **-ai before a vowel-initial word is generally replaced by -ā (rarely by -āy as within a word)**
* **-au before a vowel is generally replaced by -āv (rarely by -ā)**

Example:

:::
::: indent
⟪तस्मै⟫ + ⟪अग्नये⟫ » ⟪तस्मा⟫ ⟪अग्नये⟫ = "to this fire"
:::

### Consonant Ligatures

If two or more consonants follow immediately on each other within a word or sentence, they are written with a ligature (combined character).

1. If the first of the consonant signs to be combined ends with the vertical stroke on the right, it loses this stroke and is placed before the second consonant.

Exception: if the second consonant sign is ⟪न्⟫ or ⟪ल्⟫, this is placed under the first consonant sign, losing the horizontal stroke. Depending on the font, there are further exceptions, which are listed below. If a ligature is not provided for the relevant font, a Virāma is inserted.

⟪ख्⟩ kh: ⟪ख्य⟩ khya, ⟪ख्र⟩ khra

**⟪धर्मार्थाविरोधेन⟫ ⟪कामं⟫ ⟪सेवेत⟫, ⟪न⟫ ⟪निःसुखः⟫ ⟪स्यात्⟫ ⟪॥⟫ ⟪३⟫ ⟪॥⟫**

**⟪एको⟫ ⟪ह्यत्यासेवितो⟫ ⟪धर्मार्थकामानामात्मानमितरौ⟫ ⟪च⟫ ⟪पीदयति⟫ ⟪॥⟫ ⟪५⟫ ⟪॥⟫**

**⟪अर्थ⟫ ⟪एव⟫ ⟪प्रधान⟫ ⟪इति⟫ ⟪कौटिल्यः⟫ ⟪॥⟫ ⟪६⟫ ⟪॥⟫**

**⟪अर्थमूलौ⟫ ⟪हि⟫ ⟪धर्मकामाविति⟫ ⟪॥⟫ ⟪७⟫ ⟪॥⟫**

> Thus, let him keep his senses under control, avoid other men's women, other men's property, and violence, and avoid sleep, lust, falsehood, frivolity, uselessness, and unjust or useless business. Let him indulge in pleasure without thereby disturbing righteousness and purposeful conduct; let him not be joyless. Or let him cultivate equally all three goals of life, which are interconnected. For if one excessively devotes oneself to one of righteousness and custom, purposeful conduct, and pleasure, then that oppresses the soul and the other two goals. Kauṭilya says that purposeful conduct (**Artha**) is the most important. For righteousness and custom as well as pleasure are rooted in purposeful action.

**Translation:**
Once upon a time, there was a king named Janaka in Mithilā. He had a daughter named Sītā. She was incomparable in beauty and virtue. Many princes who wished to marry her sent messengers to Janaka.

But Janaka wished to give her to a powerful Kṣatriya prince. Therefore, he decreed that she must be "won" through heroic strength. The matter was this: He possessed an exceedingly heavy bow. Janaka promised: "Whoever lifts this bow and nocks an arrow upon it, shall marry my daughter."

When they heard this promise, princes came by the hundreds. Yet not one of them could move the bow even slightly. It is known that even Rāvaṇa, the ruler of Laṅkā, appeared full of arrogance and returned in shame. When Janaka saw that all the princes returned, he became full of worry, who would be the husband of his daughter. Meanwhile, Viśvāmitra led Rāma, the son of King Daśaratha of Ayodhyā, together with Lakṣmaṇa there. At the command of the great Ṛṣi Viśvāmitra, the splendid Rāma lifted the bow with playful ease. As soon as he nocked an arrow upon it, the bow broke into two pieces.

"Good, good!" — thus the people praised the heroic strength of the splendid Rāma.

The heart of King Janaka was exceedingly joyful. Then he summoned Daśaratha and the others and celebrated the wedding feast of Sītā and Rāma with great splendor.

**Summary:**
The fraudulent merchant in his shop could do nothing and felt only regret in his heart. Aśoka came home and told the whole incident. All relatives and friends enjoyed themselves greatly. Thus, the birthday celebration found a happy end.

# Writing Exercise 9

### Syllabification

Within a sentence (a verse half-line), syllabification in the script occurs only if a word ends with

*   Vowel
*   Anusvāra (ṃ)
*   Visarga (ḥ)

and the following word begins with a consonant. The same applies in cases where, according to the sentence sandhi rules, a hiatus arises between vowels.

### Punctuation

The end of a sentence is marked in prose with | (ardhadanda m.). In verses, | marks the end of the half-line, while || (danda m.) marks the end of the stanza. In prose, || indicates a larger break (e.g., the end of a paragraph). Verse numbering is placed between two ||, e.g., ||⟪१⟩||.

### Abbreviation

Abbreviation signs (e.g., in references to works) are °, e.g., ⟪पा⟩° = pā(ṇinīye) = "In the grammatical treatise of Pāṇini".

# Lektion 39

## 39.1. The Personal Endings of the First Person (***⟪तृतीयः⟫⟫ ⟪पुरुषः⟫ = "**third** Person")

The endings of the first person (***⟪तृतीयः⟫*** ⟪पुरुषः⟫ = "**third** Person") are:

::: grammar-box

| | ⟪परस्मैपदम्⟫ || ⟪आत्मनेपदम्⟫ ||
| :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| | ⟪एकवचनम्⟫ | ⟪बहुवचनम्⟫ | ⟪एकवचनम्⟫ | ⟪बहुवचनम्⟫ |
| **Primary endings thematic stems** | **-mi** | **-mas** | **-i**¹ | **-mahe** |
| **Primary endings athematic stems** | ^^ | ^^ | **-e** | ^^ |
| **Secondary endings thematic stems** | **-m** | **-ma** | **-i** | **-mahi** |
| **Secondary endings athematic stems** | **-am** | ^^ | ^^ | ^^ |
| **Optative ending** | ^^ | ^^ | **-a** | ^^ |
| **Perfect ending** | **-a** | ^^ | **-e** | **-mahe** |

:::
1 Note: actually, the primary ending Ā of thematic stems is also to be assumed as -e, before which the thematic vowel -a- falls away for reasons of analogy. However, the effect is as if the ending -i were to attach to the thematic vowel -a-: a + i » e.

## 39.2. Formation of the verb forms of the first person thematic present stems

::: grammar-box
**Rule:**
**Vor -mi, -mas, -ma, -mahe, -mahi wird der Themavokal -a- durch -ā- ersetzt !!!**
:::

# Lesson 29

## 29.1. Use of the Parasmaipada (⟪परस्मैपद⟫) and Ātmanepada (⟪आत्मनेपद⟫) in the Causative

::: grammar-box
**The Causative is, with few exceptions, Ubhayapada (⟪उभयपद⟫)**
:::
::: grammar-box
**In the Causative, the Ātmanepada (⟪आत्मनेपद⟫) is used:**

**1. When the result of the caused action benefits the causer:**
:::
Example:

⟪रामः⟫ ⟪कटं⟫ ⟪कारयते⟫ = "Rāma has a mat made for himself (for his own benefit)"

**2. When the causative of transitive verbs is used reflexively ("to show oneself", "to be heard", etc.), or when the object of the simple verb is the agent (⟪कर्तृ⟫) of the causative:**

Example:

⟪विष्णुर्भक्तान्दर्शयते⟫ = "Viṣṇu shows himself to his devotees"

Result: ⟪भक्ता⟫ ⟪विष्णुं⟫ ⟪पश्यन्ति⟫ = "The believers see Viṣṇu"

The rules thus generally correspond to the rules for the use of the Ātmanepada (⟪आत्मनेपद⟫) with Ubhayapada (⟪उभयपद⟫) verbs.

B) Translate and resolve the Sanskrit compounds:

⟪१⟫. **⟪गुर्वादेशाद्रामो⟫ ⟪ग्रामान्नगरं⟫ ⟪गत्वा⟫ ⟪साधुगृहं⟫ ⟪प्रविश्य⟫ ⟪साधुमुपस्थायालं⟫ ⟪क्रोधेनेति⟫ ⟪वक्ति⟫ ⟪॥१॥⟫**
At the teacher's instruction, Rāma goes from the village to the city, enters the holy man's house, respectfully presents himself before the holy man, and speaks: "Enough of anger!"

⟪२⟫. **⟪गुरोरधर्मः⟫ ⟪श्रोतुं⟫ ⟪न⟫ ⟪शक्यत⟫ ⟪इति⟫ ⟪श्रुत्या⟫ ⟪च⟫ ⟪स्मृतिभिश्चोद्यते⟫ ⟪॥२॥⟫**
The Veda (śruti) and the tradition (smṛti) say that one cannot hear anything unjust from a master.

⟪३⟫. **⟪क्षत्रिया⟫ ⟪जनाञ्छत्रुभ्यो⟫ ⟪रक्षितुमर्हन्तीति⟫ ⟪क्षत्रियधर्मः⟫ ⟪॥३॥⟫**
The duty of the Kṣatriyas is that the Kṣatriyas should protect the people from enemies.

⟪४⟫. **⟪कृतयज्ञदोषत्वाद्ब्राह्मणो⟫ ⟪धनं⟫ ⟪लब्धुं⟫ ⟪नार्ह⟫ti ⟪॥४॥⟫**
Since he has committed a sacrificial error, the Brahmin may not receive money.

⟪५⟫. **⟪धनलाभहेतोस्ते⟫ ⟪वैश्या⟫ ⟪व्रतं⟫ ⟪कृत्वा⟫ ⟪ब्रह्मचर्यं⟫ ⟪चरन्ति⟫ ⟪॥५॥⟫**
(⟪धनस्य⟫ ⟪लाभाय⟫)
In order to become rich, these Vaiśyas have made a vow and abstain sexually.

⟪६⟫. **⟪बुद्द्धाश्चार्हन्तश्च⟫ ⟪दुःखान्मुक्ताः⟫ ⟪।⟫ ⟪मुञ्चन्ती⟫ ⟪बुद्धिर्हि⟫ ⟪तैः⟫ ⟪प्राप्ता⟫ ⟪॥६॥⟫**
Buddhas and Arhants are freed from suffering. For they have attained liberating insight.

⟪७⟫. **⟪लोभ⟫en ⟪च⟫ ⟪क्रोधेन⟫ ⟪च⟫ ⟪मोहेन⟫ ⟪च⟫ ⟪जना⟫ ⟪दुष्यन्ति⟫ ⟪।⟫ ⟪ततः⟫ ⟪प्राप्तकाला⟫ ⟪नरकं⟫ ⟪पतन्ति⟫ ⟪॥७॥⟫**
Through greed, hatred, and delusion, people are ruined. When the time has come, they then fall into a hell.

## 58.6. Aorist 5: इष्-लुङ्

::: grammar-box
**The iṣ-Aorist is formed from all seṭ roots for which no other form of the Aorist is explicitly taught exclusively.**

**Formation:**

**Augment + Root + i + s + athematic secondary endings**

**!!!** The 2.sg.P and 3.sg.P derive from **-**īs and -īt respectively **!!!** (This arose from the transfer of the Imperfect from roots of the type ⟪अब्रवीत्⟩; thus, they are actually root-aorist forms).
:::
The stem-forming suffix + endings of the iṣ-Aorist are therefore:

::: grammar-box

|   | ⟪परस्मैपदम्⟫ || ⟪आत्मनेपदम्⟫ ||
| :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |
|   | ⟪एकवचनम्⟫ | ⟪बहुवचनम्⟫ | ⟪एकवचनम्⟫ | ⟪बहुवचनम्⟫ |
| **1. ⟪तृतीयः⟫** | **-iṣam** | **-iṣma** | **-iṣi** | **-iṣmahi** |
| **2. ⟪द्वितीयः⟫** | **-īs** | **-iṣṭa** | **-iṣṭhās** | **-**idhvam / :br-iḍhvam:br(wahlweise nach -h oder Halbvokal) |
| **3. ⟪प्रथमः⟫** | **-īt** | **-iṣur** | **-iṣṭa** | **-iṣata** |

:::
::: grammar-box
**Form of the root:**

*   **Roots with short vowel before a single consonant: Strong grade in P and Ā**  
    Examples:  
    ⟪बुध्⟩ 1U: 1.sg.P ⟪अबोधिषम्⟩  
    ⟪कॢप्⟩ 1Ā: 1.sg.Ā ⟪अकल्पिषि⟩

*   **Roots with final vowel:**
    *   **P: Guṇa grade**
    *   **Ā: Strong grade**

    Examples:  
    ⟪पू⟩ 9U: 1.sg.P ⟪अपाविषम्⟩ ; 1. sg.Ā ⟪अपविषि⟩

*   **Roots ending in -ar., -al, and also ⟪वद्⟩ 1P "to say", ⟪व्रज्⟩ 1P "to go away": P: Guṇa grade**  
    Examples:  
    ⟪चर्⟩ 1P: 1.sg.P ⟪अचारिषम्⟩  
    ⟪वद्⟩ 1P: 1.sg.P ⟪अवादिषम्⟩

*   **Other roots of the form (Cons.-)Cons.-a-Cons.: in P optionally Guṇa grade (does not apply to roots ending in -h, -m, -y, and some other roots)**  
    Example:  
    ⟪तन्⟩ 8U: 1.sg.P ⟪अतनिषम्⟩ / ⟪अतानिषम्⟩  
    but:  
    ⟪क्रम्⟩ 1U: 1.sg.P ⟪अक्रमिषम्⟩
:::
Paradigms:

⟪पू⟩ 9U "to purify"

**Particularities:**

1.  With some roots, the connecting vowel -i- in the ⟪आत्मनेपद⟫ can be replaced by -ī-. After ⟪ग्रह्⟫ 9U "to seize", this replacement must occur in the P and Ā:  
    ⟪अग्र⟫*⟪ही⟫*⟪षम्⟫ , ⟪अग्र⟫*⟪ही⟫*⟪षि⟫

2.  Roots of the 8th present class ending in -n (or -ṇ) can be grade-reduced in the 2.3.sg.Ā:  
    ⟪तन्⟫ 8U: 2.sg.Ā ⟪अतनिष्ठास्⟫ / ⟪अतथस्⟫ (root-aorist) ; 3. sg. Ā ⟪अतनिष्ट⟫ / ⟪अतत⟫

3.  ⟪दीप्⟫ 4Ā, ⟪जन्⟫ 4Ā, etc. can, instead of the 3.sg. Ā, also take the form of the passive aorist:  
    ⟪अदीपिष्ट⟫ / ⟪अदीपि⟫ ; ⟪अजनिष्ट⟫ / ⟪अजनि⟫

4.  ⟪विज्⟫ 7P has no ablaut:

# Lesson 9

::: deleteme-box
**In this lesson you will learn:**
- The Samāhāradvandva ("collective dvandva")
- The formation of nominal stems with the suffixes **-ka** (taddhita) and **-aka** (kṛt)
- Vocabulary related to professions and social roles
- Quotes from classical legal texts (Dharmaśāstras)
:::

## 9.1. Samāhāradvandva (⟪समाहारद्वन्द्व⟫ = "collective dvandva")

::: grammar-box
**When a dvandva is intended to express that a series of things, etc., form a unity, it generally stands in the singular neuter:**

e.g. **āhāra-nidrā-maithuna-bhayam** = ⟪आहारनिद्रामैथुनभयम्⟫ does not simply mean "food intake (**āhāra** m.), sleep (**nidrā** f.), mating (**maithuna** n.) and fear (**bhaya** n.)", but these four as a **unity** that characterizes animal life.
:::
In addition to this basic rule for the formation of Samāhāradvandvas, there are a number of other rules that can be found in Pāṇini 2,4,2-17 or e.g. Mr. R. Kale, A higher Sanskrit grammar, reprint 1969, § 189 - 192 a. In the various stages of language development, the same rules were not always observed!

## 9.2. On the Formation of Nominal Stems

### 9.2.1. -ka (taddhita)

::: grammar-box
**The taddhita suffix -ka forms among others:**

1\. **Diminutives (diminutive forms like German -chen, -lein, -li, -le):**
   **putra m. "son" » putraka m. ⟪पुत्रक⟫ "little son"**

2\. **Nouns that denote an approximate similarity:**
   **aśva m. "horse" » aśvaka m. ⟪अश्वक⟫ "little horse, a thing resembling a horse"**

3\. **Nouns without semantic difference from the underlying noun:**
   **putraka m. ⟪पुत्रक⟫ = putra m. ⟪पुत्र⟫**

4\. **Nouns that express "related to the concept of the base word":**
   **kāśi f. "Benares" » kāśika 3 ⟪काशिक⟫ "native of Benares, originating from Benares"**
   **rūpa n. "form" » rūpaka 3 ⟪रूपक⟫ "possessing the form of something"**
:::

### 9.2.2. -aka (kṛt), fem. often -ikā

::: grammar-box
**The kṛt suffix -aka, feminine often -ikā, forms agent nouns (nouns expressing the agent) from any root.**

A final vowel of the root and **-a-** at the penultimate position of the root are replaced by their lengthened grade (**vṛddhi**) (there are some exceptions), the other vowels are replaced by their strengthened grade (**guṇa**).
:::
**Examples:**

| Root:br⟪धातु⟫ | + -aka / -ikā (kṛt) | Meaning |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **kṛ** :br8 U:br⟪कृ⟫:br"machen" | **kāraka** :br(⟪कारक⟫) | "doer, making" |
| **śru** :br5 P:br⟪श्रु⟫:br"hören" | **śrāvaka** m.:br(⟪श्रावक⟫) | "hearer, student,:brbuddh.: follower of the Buddha" |
| **nī** :br1 U:br⟪नी⟫:br"führen" | **nāyaka** m.:br(⟪नायक⟫) /:br **nāyikā** f.:br(⟪नायिका⟫) | "leader, master, husband,:brlover / beloved, lady" |
| **yaj** :br1 U:br⟪यज्⟫:br"opfern" | **yājaka** m.:br(⟪याजक⟫) | "sacrificer, sacrificial priest" |
| **nṛt** :br4 P:br⟪नृत्⟫:br"tanzen" | **nartaka** m.:br(⟪नर्तक⟫) /:br **nartakī** f.:br(⟪नर्तकी⟫) | "dancer / danceress" |
| **ji** :br1 P:br⟪जि⟫:br"siegen" | **jayaka** 3:br(⟪जयक⟫) | "victorious" |

::: grammar-box
**Some of these formations have the narrower meaning: "that which habitually or as an obligation or well performs that expressed by the root".**

# Lesson 19

## 19.1. The Relative Clause

::: grammar-box

**Schema:**

**Relative pronoun -- relative clause containing the noun to which the relative clause refers -- (demonstrative pronoun) -- main clause**

**The relative clause can also stand after the main clause, but it cannot be inserted into the main clause.**

**The relative pronoun and the word it refers to, which — in contrast to German — stands in the relative clause, are in the case that the relative clause syntactically requires. The demonstrative pronoun is in the case that the main clause syntactically requires.**
:::

Examples:

Note: In relative clauses of general validity, the optative is often used instead of the indicative. Many of our examples would therefore preferably be in the optative.

**1. The agent (⟪कर्तृ⟫) of the sentence is specified further by a relative clause:**

::: indent
⟪यो⟫ ⟪नरः⟫ ⟪पुण्यं⟫ ⟪करोति⟫ ⟪स⟫ ⟪स्वर्गं⟫ ⟪गच्छति⟫ =  ⟪यो⟫ ⟪नरः⟫ ⟪पुण्यं⟫ ⟪करोति⟫ ⟪तेन⟫ ⟪स्वर्गं⟫ ⟪गम्यते⟫ = ⟪येन⟫ ⟪नरेण⟫ ⟪पुण्यम्⟫ ⟪क्रियते⟫ ⟪तेन⟫ ⟪स्वर्गं⟫ ⟪गम्यते⟫ etc. = "A man who does meritorious deeds goes to heaven."
:::
**2. The direct object (⟪कर्म⟫) of the main clause is specified further by the relative clause:**

::: indent
⟪यो⟫ ⟪ब्राह्मणो⟫ ⟪देवान्यजते⟫ ⟪तं⟫ ⟪देवा⟫ ⟪रक्षन्ति⟫ = "The gods protect a Brahmin who sacrifices to them as the sacrificer."
:::
**3. The specification of a noun of the main clause stands in the relative clause:**

::: indent
⟪ये⟫ ⟪नराः⟫ ⟪पापं⟫ ⟪कुर्वन्ति⟫ ⟪तेषां⟫ ⟪पुत्रा⟫ ⟪धनं⟫ ⟪न⟫ ⟪लभन्ते⟫ = "Sons of men who do evil do not obtain wealth."
:::
**4. Relative pronoun and word it refers to are in the genitive (⟪षष्ठी⟫):**

::: indent
⟪यस्य⟫ ⟪नरस्य⟫ ⟪पुत्राः⟫ ⟪पापं⟫ ⟪कुर्वन्ति⟫ ⟪स⟫ ⟪न⟫ ⟪सुखवान्⟫ = "The man is not happy whose sons do evil."
:::
**5. Relative pronoun and word it refers to are in the instrumental (⟪तृतीया⟫):**

::: indent
⟪येन⟫ ⟪शत्रुणा⟫ ⟪ग्रामो⟫ ⟪जितस्तं⟫ ⟪द्विषन्ति⟫ = "They hate the enemy who has conquered / captured their village."
:::
**6. Relative pronoun and word it refers to are in the accusative (⟪द्वितीया⟫):**

::: indent
⟪यं⟫ ⟪नरं⟫ ⟪देवी⟫ ⟪रक्षति⟫ ⟪स⟫ ⟪सुखमाप्नोति⟫ = "A man whom the goddess protects attains happiness."
:::

## 48.3. On nominal derivation: ⟪तद्धित⟫-suffixes -a and -ya

::: grammar-box
With the suffix **-a** and (less frequently) **-ya**, a noun can be derived from another noun. In this process, the first syllable of the original noun receives the guṇa grade (**⟪वृद्धि⟫**). If the original stem already ends in **-a**, then the **⟪वृद्धि⟫** is the only marker of derivation, since the final sound of the stem remains unchanged.

The derived words have the meaning:

> "having some relation to that designated by the base word"

e.g.

*   "originating from"
*   "belonging to"

The words formed in this way are adjectives, but can be substantivized, e.g. as patronymics (name formation after the father: "son of N.N.") or abstract nouns (mostly neuter).
:::
Examples:

::: indent
| Base word | Derivation |
| :--- | :--- |
| **⟪शुचि⟫** 3 "shining, pure" | **⟪शौच⟫** n. "purity" |
| **⟪पुत्र⟫** m. "son" | **⟪पौत्र⟫** m. "originating from the son = grandson" |
| **⟪गोतम⟫** m. "owner of many cows" proper name | **⟪गौतम⟫** m. "son of Gotama" |
| **⟪ब्रह्मन्⟫** n. "formulated truth, Veda, Absolute" | **⟪ब्राह्मण⟫** m. "formulator of truth, Brāhmaṇa" |
| **⟪शूर⟫** 3 "heroic" | **⟪शौर्य⟫** n. "heroism, bravery" |
| **⟪राजन्⟫** m. "king" | **⟪राज्य⟫** n. "kingship" |
| **⟪देव⟫** m. "Heavenly, god" | **⟪दैव्य⟫** 3 "heavenly" |
| **⟪ग्राम⟫** m. "village" | **⟪ग्राम्य⟫** 3 "village-like" |
:::
::: grammar-box
| **Treatment of the stem final before the suffix \-a:** ||
| :---: | :--- |
| **\-ṛ** | **\-a** generally attaches to the final **\-r**:br e.g. ⟪जेतृ⟫ "winner" » ⟪जैत्र⟫ 3 "victorious" |
| **\-a** | Replacement of the base word's **\-a** by the new suffix **\-a**. :br Examples see above. |
| **\-i** | Loss of the **\-i** :br e.g. ⟪प्रकृति⟫ f. "nature" » ⟪प्राकृत⟫ 3 "natural, normal, customary, vulgar" |
| **\-u** | mostly: **\-av-a** :br e.g. ⟪गुरु⟫ 3 "heavy"; m. "master, teacher" » ⟪गौरव⟫ 3 "belonging to the master, originating from the teacher"; n. "weight, heaviness, dignity" |
| **other declension stems:** | see Wackernagel, Altind. Grammatik II,2 § 38 |

Before the suffix **-ya**, the stem final is treated similarly to before the suffix **-a**.
:::
See examples above!

::: grammar-box
**Derivations can also be formed from compounds using these suffixes.**

e.g. **⟪स्वश्व⟫** m. "he, whose horses are good" proper name » **⟪सौवश्व⟫** m. "Descendant of Svaśva"

**In compounds, where due to Sandhi the final -i or -u of the first member is replaced by -y or -v and thus precede the first vowel of the base word (e.g. compounds with ni-, vi-, su-), the ⟪वृद्धि⟫ is formed as if -iy or -uv were present.**

e.g. **⟪व्याघ्र⟫** m. "Tiger" » **⟪वैयाघ्र⟫** 3 "descended from a tiger, belonging to a tiger"

Lesson 61 forms the conclusion of the Sanskrit course and contains no further written exercises.

⟪५⟫. **⟪क्रयेण⟫ ⟪च⟫ ⟪विक्रयेण⟫ ⟪च⟫ ⟪वैश्या⟫ ⟪जीवेयुरिति⟫ ⟪वैश्यधर्मः⟫ ⟪।⟫ ⟪एवं⟫ ⟪सति⟫ ⟪वैश्यपुत्राः⟫ ⟪क्रीणन्ति⟫ ⟪विक्रीणते⟫ ⟪च⟫ ⟪॥५॥⟫**
(⟪वैश्यानां⟫ ⟪पुत्राः⟫)
It is the duty of the Vaiśyas to make a living from buying and selling. Therefore, Vaiśyas buy and sell.

⟪६⟫. **⟪कृतपापो⟫ ⟪नरश्चेन्नरके⟫ ⟪पापात्पूतः⟫ ⟪स्यात्पुनर्भवं⟫ ⟪गच्छेत्⟫ ⟪॥६॥⟫**
(⟪कृतं⟫ ⟪पापं⟫ ⟪येन⟫ ⟪सः⟫ ⟪।⟫ ⟪पुनर्भव⟫ — ⟪पुनः⟫ ⟪भवति⟫ ⟪इति⟫)
When a wrongdoer has been purified of his wickedness in a hell, he is reborn.

⟪७⟫. **⟪ब्राह्मणपुत्रा⟫ ⟪वेदाध्यायांश्च⟫ ⟪स्मृत्यध्यायांश्च⟫ ⟪पुनः⟫ ⟪पुनरधीयीरन्नित्यार्यधर्मः⟫ ⟪॥७॥⟫**
(⟪ब्राह्मणानां⟫ ⟪पुत्राः⟫ ⟪।⟫ ⟪वेदानामध्यायांश्च⟫ ⟪स्मृतीनामध्यायांश्च⟫)
It is the duty of the nobles that sons of Brahmins repeatedly study the sections of the Vedas and the tradition.

⟪८⟫. **⟪यो⟫ ⟪ब्राह्मणः⟫ ⟪शूद्रां⟫ ⟪कामयेत⟫ ⟪स⟫ ⟪सद्ब्राह्मणो⟫ ⟪न⟫ ⟪स्यात्⟫ ⟪।⟫ ⟪सद्ब्राह्मणो⟫ ⟪हि⟫ ⟪ब्राह्मणीं⟫ ⟪कामयेत⟫ ⟪॥८॥⟫**
(⟪सन्⟫-⟪ब्राह्मणः⟫)
Ein Brahmane, der eine Śūdra liebt, ist kein guter Brahmane, denn ein guter Brahmane liebt eine Brahmanin.

⟪९⟫. **⟪सत्यं⟫ ⟪ब्रूयात्प्रियं⟫ ⟪ब्रूयान्न⟫ ⟪ब्रूयात्सत्यमप्रियम्⟫ ⟪।⟫**  
**⟪प्रियं⟫ ⟪च⟫ ⟪नानृतं⟫ ⟪ब्रूयादेष⟫ ⟪धर्मः⟫ ⟪सनातनः⟫ ⟪॥९॥⟫** (Manu IV.138)  
Speak truths that are pleasant; do not speak unpleasant truths; do not speak pleasant untruths; this is the eternal law.

## 59.5. Aorist (⟪लुङ्⟫) 6: sइष्-लुङ् (P only)

::: grammar-box
**The siṣ-Aorist is formed in the P by all roots ending in -ā, -e, -o, -ai, which are not restricted to the 1st, 2nd, or 3rd Aorist, as well as by several other roots, including ⟪नम्⟫, ⟪यम्⟫, ⟪रम्⟫. In the Ā, all these roots form the s-Aorist.**

**Formation:**

**Augment + strong-grade root + s + i + ṣ + athematic secondary endings (as in iṣ-Aorist)**
:::
Thus, the stem-forming suffix + endings of the siṣ-Aorist are:

::: grammar-box
|   | ⟪परस्मैपदम्⟫ |||
| :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: |
|   | ⟪एकवचनम्⟫ | ⟪द्विवचनम्⟫ | ⟪बहुवचनम्⟫ |
| **1. ⟪तृतीयः⟫** | **-siṣam** | **-siṣva** | **-siṣma** |
| **2. ⟪द्वितीयः⟫** | **-sīs** | **-siṣṭam** | **-siṣṭa** |
| **3. ⟪प्रथमः⟫** | **-sīt** | **-siṣṭām** | **-siṣur** |
:::

## 59.6. लुङ् ७: स-लुङ् (स-लुङ् सस्वरः)

::: grammar-box
**The sa-Aorist is formed by most ⟪अनिट्⟫ roots ending in -ś, -ṣ, or -h, with i, u, or ṛ in the penultimate position. Optional ⟪अनिट्⟫ roots of this form may optionally form either the sa-Aorist or the iṣ-Aorist.**

**Formation:**

**Augment + weak-grade root + s + a + thematic secondary endings**

**The 1.sg, 2.du, 3.du, and Ā are formed from the s-Aorist, i.e., athematically.**
:::
Thus, the stem-forming suffix + endings of the sa-Aorist are:

::: grammar-box
|   | ⟪परस्मैपदम्⟫ ||| ⟪आत्मनेपदम्⟫ |||

| **1. ⟪तृतीयः⟫** | **-sam** | **-sāva** | **-sāma** | **-si** | **-sāvahī** | **-sāmahi** |
| **2. ⟪द्वितीयः⟫** | **-sas** | **-satam** | **-sata** | **-sathās** | **-sāthām** | **-sadhvam** |
| **3. ⟪प्रथमः⟫** | **-sat** | **-satām** | **-san** | **-sata** | **-sātām** | **-santa** |
:::

# Lesson 8

::: deleteme-box
**In this lesson you will learn:**
- The formation of nouns (kṛt- and taddhita suffixes)
- Important nominal suffixes (-a, -ana, -tra, -ti, -tva, -tā)
- The 8th present class (tanādi)
- The conjugation of **kṛ** (tun, to make)
:::

## 8.1. On the Formation of Nouns

In traditional Indian grammar, a distinction is made among the suffixes used to form nominal stems:

- **kṛt suffixes (⟪कृत्⟫) (primary suffixes):** form nominal stems, absolutes, and infinitives from verbal roots (**dhātu** m. = ⟪धातु⟫) and verbal stems.
- **taddhita suffixes (⟪तद्धित⟫) (secondary suffixes):** attach to nominal stems and indeclinables to form new nominal stems or indeclinables.

::: grammar-box
**Schema:**
**Root + kṛt suffix » nominal stem etc. + taddhita suffix » new nominal stem etc.**

**Nominal stem + case ending » syntactically functional noun**
:::

## 8.2. Classification of Nominal Suffixes

- **kṛt (kṛdanta) = ⟪कृत्⟫ (⟪कृदन्त⟫)**
  - **kārakakṛt** (⟪कारककृत्⟫) » nomina agentis (denote someone who performs the action indicated by the root)
  - **kṛtikṛt** (⟪कृतिकृत्⟫) » nomina actionis (denote the action expressed by the root) or abstracts

- **taddhita**
  - **viśeṣyataddhita** (⟪विशेष्यतद्धित⟫) » adjectives
  - **bhāvārthakataddhita (tanmātrataddhita)** (⟪भावार्थकतद्धित⟫ / ⟪तन्मात्रतद्धित⟫) » abstracts
  - **tadvattaddhita** (⟪तद्वत्तद्धित⟫) » possessive (e.g., **-mant** -⟪मन्त्⟫, **-vant** -⟪वन्त्⟫)
  - **tolanataddhita (atiśāyanataddhita)** (⟪तोलनतद्धित⟫ / ⟪अतिशायनतद्धित⟫) » comparison (comparative, superlative), comparison
  - **pūraṇataddhita** (⟪पूरणतद्धित⟫) » ordinal numbers (first, etc.)
  - **vibhaktitaddhita** (⟪विभक्तितद्धित⟫) » in place of case endings (e.g., **-tas** -⟪तस्⟫, **-tra** -⟪त्र⟫)
  - **abhūtatadbhāva (cvitaddhita)** (⟪अभूततद्भाव⟫ / ⟪च्वितद्धित⟫) » (cvi formations ⟪च्वि⟫, **-sāt** -⟪सात्⟫)

**Classification based on ablaut:**
- **guṇya** (⟪गुण्य⟫): strong-grade formation
- **na guṇya** (⟪न⟫ ⟪गुण्य⟫): weak-grade formation
- **vṛddhyarha** (⟪वृद्ध्यर्ह⟫): lengthened-grade formation

## 8.3. Some Important Nominal Suffixes

### 8.3.1. -a m. (kṛt)

::: grammar-box
**The kṛt suffix -a forms masculine (rarely neuter) nouns that denote an action or state indicated by the root; sometimes also adjectives or nouns that express the agent (kartṛ) of the action denoted by the verbal root. For short penults (= vowel before the consonant at which the root ends) or final root vowels, strong grade (guṇa) or lengthened grade (vṛddhi) is usually substituted.**
:::
**Examples:**

| Root:br⟪धातु⟫ | + -a (kṛt) | Meaning |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **ji** 1 P:br⟪आप्⟫:br"siegen" | **jaya** m.:br⟪जय⟫ | "conquering, victory" |
| **muh** 4 P:br⟪मुह्⟫:br"verwirrt sein" | **moha** m.:br⟪मोह⟫ | "confusion, delusion, error" |

| **kup** 4 P:br⟪कुप्⟫:br"zürnen" | **kopa** m.:br⟪कोप⟫ | "anger" |
| **lubh** 4 P:br⟪लुभ्⟫:br"begehren" | **lobha** m.:br⟪लोभ⟫ | "desire" |

### 8.3.2. -ana n. (kṛt)

::: grammar-box
**The kṛt suffix -ana usually forms neuter nouns that denote an action, a state, or the means or instrument by which the action designated by the root or verbal stem is accomplished. For a short penultimate or an ending vowel of the root, usually the strong grade (guṇa) is substituted.**
:::
**Examples:**

| Root:br⟪धातु⟫ | + -ana (kṛt) | Meaning |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **gam** 1 P:br⟪गम्⟫:br"gehen" | **gamana** n.:br⟪गमन⟫ | "going" |
| **nī** 1 U:br⟪नी⟫:br"führen" | **nayana** n.:br⟪नयन⟫ | "(the instrument of leading, i.e.) eye" |
| **śru** 5 P:br⟪श्रु⟫:br"hören" | **śravaṇa** n.:br⟪श्रवण⟫ | "(hearing instrument =) ear" |
| **kṛ** 8 U:br⟪कृ⟫:br"tun" | **kāraṇa** n.:br⟪कारण⟫ | "(that by which something is done, i.e.) cause, reason" |
| **bhū** 1 P:br⟪भू⟫:br"werden" | **bhavana** n.:br⟪भवन⟫ | "becoming, arising" |
| **dṛś** 4 P:br⟪दृश्⟫:br"sehen" | **darśana** n.:br⟪दर्शन⟫ | "seeing, viewpoint, philosophical system, appearance, specifically: Darśan" |

::: note-box
**"Darshan"** or **"Darshana"** is a term from Hinduism for the sight and vision of the sacred and divine. Under *Darshana* is understood, for example, the official meeting of student and teacher, in which the student was invited by the teacher. However, it can also mean *immersing oneself* while contemplating an image of a deity. The latter meaning is the one that is most common in modern Hindi usage. In connection with Mata Amritanandamayi, Darshan means the embrace by the Guru.

Devout Hindus go to the temple to obtain the sight of God through a symbol or statue, in which the spiritual presence of the deity is assumed. In this sense, also a blessing by the deity. However, Darshan can also be received through a vision of the deity during prayer or meditation. Also, a living person who is regarded as an incarnation of the deity, such as an Avatara, can give Darshan.
(Source: Wikipedia)
:::

### 8.3.3. -tra n. (kṛt)

::: grammar-box
**The kṛt suffix -tra forms (mostly) neuter nouns that denote the means or instrument by which the action designated by the root comes about. A short penultimate and final vowel of the root is replaced by strong grade (guṇa).**
:::

**Examples:**

| Root:br⟪धातु⟫ | + -tra (kṛt) | Meaning |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **nī** 1 U:br⟪नी⟫:br"führen" | **netra** n.:br⟪नेत्र⟫ | "(Means of leading =) eye" |

### 8.3.4. -ti f. (kṛt)

::: grammar-box
**The kṛt suffix -ti forms feminine nouns that generally express the action designated by the root or the state designated by the root. The form of the root is in the weak grade.**
:::
**Examples:**

| Root:br⟪धातु⟫ | + -ti (kṛt) | Meaning |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **śru** 5 P:br⟪श्रु⟫:br"hören" | **śruti** f.:br⟪श्रुति⟫ | "hearing, the Veda" |
| **smṛ** 1 P:br⟪स्मृ⟫:br"vergegenwärtigen" | **smṛti** f.:br⟪स्मृति⟫ | "recalling, memory, tradition, mindfulness" |
| **nī** 1 U:br⟪नी⟫:br"führen" | **nīti** f.:br⟪नीति⟫ | "leading, guidance, conduct" |
| **sṛj** 6 P:br⟪सृज्⟫:br"emanieren lassen" | **sṛṣṭi** f.:br⟪सृष्टि⟫ | "emanation, creation" |
| **dṛś** 4 P:br⟪दृश्⟫:br"sehen" | **dṛṣṭi** f.:br⟪दृष्टि⟫ | "sight, face, viewpoint" |
| **gam** 1 P:br⟪गम्⟫:br"gehen" | **gati** f.:br⟪गति⟫ | "going, course, goal of going" (from *gm » ga + -ti) |
| **man** 4 Ā:br⟪मन्⟫:br"denken" | **mati** f.:br⟪मति⟫ | "thinking, thought, opinion" (from *mn » ma + -ti) |

*Note: \* before a form means that this form does not occur in Sanskrit, but is theoretically reconstructed as a prerequisite for a specific formation. The weak grade of **gam** is gṃ = \*gm, the m is replaced by **a** as a so-called sonant nasal » **ga**. The same applies to **man** » **ma**.

### 8.3.5. -tva n., -tā f. (taddhita)

::: grammar-box
**The taddhita suffixes -tva n. and -tā f. form abstract nouns from nouns. The form of the underlying nominal stem remains unchanged.**
:::
**Examples:**

| Nominalstamm:br⟪नामप्रातिपदिक⟫ | + -tva n.:br(taddhita) | + -tā f.:br(taddhita) | Meaning |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **guru** :br⟪गुरु⟫:br3 "schwer, würdig,:brm. Meister" | **gurutva** n.:br⟪गुरुत्व⟫ | **gurutā** f.:br⟪गुरुता⟫ | "heaviness, reverence,:brteacherhood (essence or nature of a teacher)" |
| **brāhmaṇa** :br⟪ब्राह्मण⟫:brm. "Brahmane" | **brāhmaṇatva** n.:br⟪ब्राह्मणत्व⟫ | **brāhmaṇatā** f.:br⟪ब्राह्मणता⟫ | "das Brahmane-sein,:brwas einen Brahmanen zum Brahmanen macht,:brWesen / Natur eines Brahmanen" |
| **deva** :br⟪देव⟫:brm. "Himmlischer, Gott" | — | **devatā** f.:br⟪देवता⟫ | "deity" |

These formations can be practically created for any noun and are very common in scientific Sanskrit works.

## 8.4. The 8th Present Class (tanādi = ⟪तनादि⟫ = "tan etc.")
7d374325e856240cba39dfa3bc4ddcd4:
::: grammar-box
**Stem Formation:**
- **Strong Stem: Root + -o-**
- **Weak Stem: Root + -u- (before vowel: -v-)**

Example **tan** 8 U (⟪तन्⟫) "to stretch":
- 3\. sg. P. **tanoti** :br⟪तनोति⟫
- 3\. pl. P. **tanvanti** :br⟪तन्वन्ति⟫
- 3\. sg. Ā. **tanute** :br⟪तनुते⟫
- 3\. pl. Ā. **tanvate** :br⟪तन्वते⟫
:::
Note: Regarding the debate on whether **tan** is actually a root of the 5th class (*tn » ta + no-), see Thumb-Hauschild, Handbuch des Sanskrit II, 265.

The most important root of the 8th class is **kṛ** 8 U (⟪कृ⟫) "to do, to make". Its conjugation is irregular:

::: grammar-box
**kṛ 8 U (⟪कृ⟫) "to make, to do"**
- 3\. sg. P. **karoti** :br⟪करोति⟫
- 3\. pl. P. **kurvanti** :br⟪कुर्वन्ति⟫
- 3\. sg. Ā. **kurute** :br⟪कुरुते⟫
- 3\. pl. Ā. **kurvate** :br⟪कुर्वते⟫
:::

# Lesson 18

## 18.1. ⟪सुभाषितम्⟫

::: indent
⟪नास्ति⟫ ⟪कामसमो⟫ ⟪व्याधिर्⟫  
⟪नास्ति⟫ ⟪मोहसमो⟫ ⟪रिपुः⟫ ⟪।⟫  
⟪नास्ति⟫ ⟪क्रोधसमो⟫ ⟪वह्निर्⟫  
⟪नास्ति⟫ ⟪ज्ञानसमं⟫ ⟪सुखम्⟫ ⟪॥⟫
:::
## 18.2. Determinative compounds (⟪तत्पुरुष⟫) with adverbial first member

As an adverbial (indeclinable) first member, the following can be used:

*   adverbs
*   prepositions
*   particles
*   other indeclinables

::: indent
can be used. Such Tatpuruṣa compounds mostly belong to the class of Nityasamāsa = ⟪नित्यसमास⟫ (m. "permanent compound"), i.e., compounds that cannot be resolved at all or not merely by means of the words occurring in the compound itself.
:::
Examples:

⟪अति⟫ "beyond that":

::: indent
⟪अतिगुरु⟫ 3: extremely heavy, extremely weighty

⟪अतिपुरुष⟫ m.: outstanding man, Superman, hero

⟪अतिस्तुति⟫ f.: excessive praise

⟪अत्युक्ति⟫ f.: excessive speech, exaggeration
:::
The most important adverbial first members are a-/an-, su-, dus-.

⟪अ⟫ (before consonant), ⟪अन्⟫ (before vowel): un-: stands in the compound instead of ⟪न⟫ "not".

Examples:

::: indent
⟪अनृत⟫ n. = ⟪नर्तम्⟫ (= ⟪न⟫ + ⟪ऋतम्⟫): untruth, lie

⟪अकृत⟫ 3 = ⟪न⟫ ⟪कृत⟫ 3: not done, undone

⟪अब्राह्मणी⟫ f. = ⟪न⟫ ⟪ब्राह्मणी⟫ : a non-Brahmin woman, un-Brahmin

⟪अदेव⟫ m. = ⟪न⟫ ⟪देवः⟫ : a non-god, un-god
:::
⟪सु⟫ "well, good"; when resolving the compound, commentators replace it with an adjective meaning "good" (e.g., ⟪सुष्टु⟫ 3, ⟪शोभन⟫ 3).

Examples:

::: indent
⟪सुकवि⟫ m.: a good poet

⟪सुकृत⟫ n.: good deed

⟪सुखादित⟫ 3: well chewed

⟪सुदुःख⟫ n.: great suffering
:::
⟪दुस्⟫ "bad, evil" (observe Sandhi!).

Examples:

::: indent
⟪दुर्नय⟫ m.: bad guidance, bad behavior

⟪दुष्करण⟫ n.: bad deed, difficult deed
:::
The following rule applies here:

::: grammar-box

Sound change of -s in compounds

Contrary to sentence Sandhi, in the final position of the first member of compounds:

\-s after -i- or -u- before voiceless guttural or labial » -ṣ

Therefore: ⟪दुष्करण⟫

:::
### 18.2.1. Compounds of the type ⟪सुकर⟫ / ⟪दुष्कर⟫

::: grammar-box

Compounds of the type ⟪सुकर⟫ / ⟪दुष्कर⟫ mainly have the meaning of passive possibility:

Examples:

:::
::: indent
⟪सुकर⟫ 3: easy to do

⟪सुगम⟫ 3: easy to go

⟪दुर्गम⟫ 3: difficult to go

⟪सुदुर्गम⟫ 3: very difficult to go
:::
### 18.2.2. Meanings of nañ-Tatpuruṣa (a- / an-)

Tatpuruṣa with a- / an- can have the following meanings:

1.  Similarity (⟪तत्सादृश्यम्⟫):  
    ⟪अब्राह्मणः⟫ = a Kṣatriya or Vaiśya who wears the sacred thread (⟪यज्ञोपवीत⟫ n.) and thus resembles a Brahmin, without being one
2.  Absence, non-existence (⟪तदभावः⟫):  
    ⟪अज्ञानम्⟫ = ignorance (absence of knowledge)
3.  Otherness (⟪तदन्यत्वम्⟫):  
    ⟪अपटम्⟫ = something that is not fabric / garment (⟪पट⟫ m: fabric, garment)
4.  Smallness (⟪तदल्पता⟫):  
    ⟪अनुदरम्⟫ = a small belly (a non-belly)
5.  Disapproval (⟪अप्राशास्त्यम्⟫):  
    ⟪अकालः⟫ = unseasonal time
6.  Hostility (⟪निरोधः⟫):  
    ⟪असुरः⟫ = counter-god (according to the false etymology a-sura)

The following verse summarizes these meanings:

⟪तदन्यत्वं⟫ ⟪तदल्पता⟫ ⟪।⟫  
⟪अप्राशास्त्यं⟫ ⟪निरोधश्च⟫  
⟪नजर्थाः⟫ ⟪षट्प्रकीर्तिताः⟫ ⟪॥⟫

## 18.3. Verbal Compounds

::: indent
⟪उपसर्गेण⟫ ⟪धात्वर्थो⟫  
⟪बलादन्यत्र⟫ ⟪नीयते⟫ ⟪।⟫  
⟪गङ्गासलिलमाधुर्यं⟫  
⟪सागरेण⟫ ⟪यथाम्भसा⟫ ⟪॥⟫
:::
⟪चन्द्रकीर्ति⟫ : ⟪प्रसन्नपदा⟫ p. 2 line 14f.

A prefix forcibly changes the meaning of a root, just as the sweetness of the Ganges water is changed by seawater.

::: grammar-box

Verbs in Sanskrit can be combined with prefixes (⟪उपसर्ग⟫ m.). In most cases, sentence sandhi applies. Prefixes can, under certain circumstances, significantly modify the meaning of the root, so that in many cases the meaning of a root with a prefix must be learned separately. Verbs with a prefix may have a different mood (P, Ā) than the simple root. Multiple prefixes can be placed before a root simultaneously.

:::
Some important prefixes are:

⟪उप⟫ "to, towards, against"

Examples:

::: indent
⟪उपगम्⟫ 1 ⟪उपगच्छति⟫ : to go towards, to approach

⟪उपदिश्⟫ 6 ⟪उपदिशति⟫ : to point out, to instruct, to advise

⟪उपपद्⟫ 4 Ā ⟪उपपद्यते⟫ : to reach, to arrive

*   PPP ⟪उपपन्न⟫ 3: equipped with (Instrumental)

⟪उपलभ्⟫ 1 Ā ⟪उपलभते⟫ : to grasp, to attain
:::
⟪प्र⟫ "forward, forth"

Examples:

::: indent
⟪प्राप्⟫ (pra-āp) 5 ⟪प्राप्नोति⟫ : to attain

⟪प्रदिश्⟫ 6 ⟪प्रदिशति⟫ : to show

⟪प्रबुध्⟫ 4 Ā ⟪प्रबुध्यते⟫ : to wake up, to recognize

⟪प्रभू⟫ 1 ⟪प्रभवति⟫ : to emerge, to stand out, to have power over (Gen., Loc. Dat.)

⟪प्रवच्⟫ 2 ⟪प्रवक्ति⟫ PPP ⟪प्रोक्त⟫ (« pra + ukta) : to explain, to communicate, to utter

⟪प्रवद्⟫ 1 ⟪प्रवदति⟫ : to utter, to designate as, to declare to be

⟪प्रस्तु⟫ 2 ⟪प्रस्तौति⟫ : to praise before, to praise loudly, to mention something, to begin
:::
⟪वि⟫ "apart, away, apart, dis-, vi-"

Examples:

::: indent
⟪विगम्⟫ 1 ⟪विगच्छति⟫ : to go apart, to pass away, to disappear

⟪विजि⟫ 1 Ā (!) ⟪विजयते⟫ : to conquer

⟪विमुच्⟫ 6 ⟪विमुञ्चति⟫ : to detach, to liberate

⟪विवद्⟫ 1 ⟪विवदति⟫ : to dispute, to discuss, to tell

⟪विस्मृ⟫ 1 ⟪विस्मरति⟫ : to forget

⟪विहन्⟫ 2 ⟪विहन्ति⟫ : to shatter, to destroy, to annihilate
:::
⟪सम्⟫ "together, with"

Examples:

::: indent
⟪समास्⟫ 2 Ā ⟪समास्ते⟫ : to sit together, to stay, to dwell

⟪समि⟫ 2 ⟪समेति⟫ : to come together, to unite

⟪संगम्⟫ 1 Ā (!) ⟪संगच्छते⟫ : to come together, to meet (friendly or hostile), to have sexual intercourse with (Acc.)

⟪संजन्⟫ 4 Ā ⟪संजायते⟫ : to arise

*   PPP ⟪संजात⟫ 3: born, arisen, become

⟪सम्बुध्⟫ 4 Ā ⟪सम्बुध्यते⟫ : to awaken completely (to the truth)

⟪सम्पद्⟫ 4 Ā ⟪सम्पद्यते⟫ : to be granted to someone, to succeed

*   PPP ⟪सम्पन्न⟫ 3: provided with (Instr.)
:::
::: grammar-box

The root ⟪कृ⟫ "to do" shows, in combination with the prefixes ⟪सम्⟫ ⟪।⟫ ⟪उप⟫ ⟪।⟫ ⟪अप⟫ ⟪।⟫ ⟪परि⟫ also the form ⟪स्कृ⟫

:::
Example:

::: indent
sam-kṛ 8 ⟪संस्करोति⟫ : to prepare, to prepare for sacrifice, to consecrate

*   PPP ⟪संस्कृत⟫ 3: prepared for the sacrifice ; ⟪संस्कृत⟫ n.: Sanskrit: the language suitable for the sacrifice ; counterpart ⟪प्राकृत⟫ 3: ordinary, common ; ⟪प्राकृत⟫ n.: ordinary language, Prakrit (designation for the vernacular and trade languages related to Sanskrit)

## 18.4. Vocabulary list

⟪सुष्टु⟫ 3: highly praised, excellent, good

## 49.3. Nominal Derivation: ⟪कृत्⟫ Suffix -as Neuter

With the ⟪कृत्⟫ suffix -as Neuter, numerous nouns are formed. Most of these are abstract nouns or nomina actionis (words that denote the action).

Short vowel of the root before a simple consonant as well as word-final root vowel appear in the strong grade.

Examples:

::: grammar-box
| Root | Nomen auf -as |
| --- | --- |
| ⟪मन्⟫ 4Ā "to think" | ⟪मनस्⟫ n. "thinking, thought, organ of thought" |
| ⟪नम्⟫ 1P "to bend" | ⟪नमस्⟫ n. "bowing, reverence" |
| ⟪चित्⟫ 1P "to perceive, to think" | ⟪चेतस्⟫ n. "insight" |
:::
Nouns on -is and -us are relatively rare.

**⟪गृहस्तस्य⟫ ⟪स्वधर्माजीवस्तुल्यैरसमानार्षिभिर्वैवाह्यमृतुगाित्वं⟫ ⟪देवपित्रातिथिपूजा⟫ ⟪भृत्येषु⟫ ⟪त्यागः⟫ ⟪शेषभोजनं⟫ ⟪च⟫ ⟪॥⟫ ⟪९⟫ ⟪॥⟫**

> A householder should:
> * have a livelihood corresponding to his specific dharma
> * enter into a marriage connection with persons of equal standing from another Gotra (Ṛṣi)
> * have sexual intercourse with his wife during her fertile times
> * honor gods, forefathers, and guests
> * be generous toward those dependent on him
> * and eat what remains.

**⟪ब्रह्मचारिणः⟫ ⟪स्वाध्यायो⟫ ⟪ऽग्निकार्याभिषेकौ⟫ ⟪भैक्षाव्रतित्वमाचार्ये⟫ ⟪प्राणान्तिकी⟫ ⟪वृत्तिस्तदभावे⟫ ⟪गुरुपुत्रे⟫ ⟪सब्रह्मचारिणि⟫ ⟪वा⟫ ⟪॥⟫ ⟪१०⟫ ⟪॥⟫**

> A celibate Vedic student should:
> study the Veda
> * ritually tend the fire
> * perform sprinkling rites
> * keep the vow to live on alms-food
> * reside with the Ācārya and care for him until his death, or with the master's son or with a fellow student.

**⟪वानप्रस्थस्य⟫ ⟪ब्रह्मचर्यं⟫ ⟪भूमौ⟫ ⟪शय्या⟫ ⟪जाटाजिनधारणमग्निहोत्राभिषेकौ⟫ ⟪देवतापित्रतिथिपूजा⟫ ⟪वन्यश्चाहारः⟫ ⟪॥⟫ ⟪११⟫ ⟪॥⟫**

> A forest-dweller should:
> * live celibately
> * lie on the ground
> * wear braided hair and an antelope skin
> * perform fire sacrifices and sprinkling rites
> * honor gods, forefathers, and guests
> * nourish himself with forest products.

**⟪प्रव्राजकस्य⟫ ⟪जितेन्द्रियत्वमनारम्भो⟫ ⟪निष्किंचनत्वं⟫ ⟪सङ्गत्यागो⟫ ⟪भैक्षाव्रतमनेकत्रारण्ये⟫ ⟪च⟫ ⟪वासो⟫ ⟪बाह्याभ्यन्तरं⟫ ⟪च⟫ ⟪शौचम्⟫ ⟪॥⟫ ⟪१२⟫ ⟪॥⟫**

> A homeless wandering ascetic should:
> * conquer his senses
> * begin nothing new
> * be without any possession
> * abandon all attachment
> * keep the vow to live on alms-food
> * dwell in many places in the wilderness
> * be pure inwardly and outwardly.

## 38.2. Sound change of nasals in words

::: grammar-box
Nasals in words are assimilated to following consonants, i.e., they are replaced by the nasal corresponding to that consonant.

After c- and j-, -n- is replaced by -ñ-.
:::
## 38.3. Declension of stems ending in -n

### 38.3.1. Nouns ending in -an as well as nouns ending in -man or -van after a vowel
::: grammar-box
Nouns ending in **-an** as well as nouns ending in **-man** or **-van** after a vowel have three stems:

| Stem | -an | -man | -van | Usage |
| :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :--- |
| **Strong Stem** | **-ān** | **-mān** | **-vān** | Nom., Acc., Voc. sg. m. f.:brNom., Acc., Voc. dual m. f.:brNom., Voc. pl. m. f.:brNom., Acc. pl. n. |
| **Medium Weak Stem** | **-a** :br(from -*n) | **-ma** :br(from -*mn) | **-va** :br(from -*vn) | Remaining cases before consonant-initial endings:brOptionally also Loc. sg. m. n. f. |
| **Weakest Stem** | **-n** | **-mn** | **-vn** | Remaining cases before vowel-initial endings |

**The endings are regular. The nominative singular m. f. is formed without final -n.**
:::
Examples:

⟪राजन्⟫ m. "king"

*   strong stem: ⟪राजान्⟫
*   middle stem: ⟪राज⟫
*   weakest stem: ⟪राज्ञ्⟫

⟪सीमन्⟫ f. "boundary"

*   strong stem: ⟪सीमान्⟫
*   middle stem: ⟪सीम⟫
*   weakest stem: ⟪सीम्न्⟫

⟪नामन्⟫ n. "name"

*   strong stem: ⟪नामान्⟫
*   middle stem: ⟪नाम⟫
*   weakest stem: ⟪नाम्न्⟫
::: grammar-box

### 38.3.3. Masculines and Neuters in -in, -min, -vin

::: grammar-box
These nouns have **no** stem gradation.

Nom.sg.m. and Nom.Akk.pl.n. are formed by analogy to the -an stems (lengthening of the -i-), as is the stem in **\-i-** before a consonantal ending.

The feminine is formed with the suffix -ī: e.g. ⟪बलिनी⟫
:::

## 38.4. On nominal formation: ⟪तद्धित⟫-suffix -in

::: grammar-box
With the (very important!) ⟪तद्धित⟫-suffix **-in**, adjectives are formed from nouns with the meaning:

**characterized by, possessing**

Originally, the formation with the suffix **-⟪इन्⟫** differed from that with **-⟪मन्त्⟫/-⟪वन्त्⟫** in that **-⟪इन्⟫** denoted characterization by something special, whereas **-⟪मन्त्⟫/-⟪वन्त्⟫** expressed possession of, or characterization by, something ordinary or general.
:::
Example:

⟪हस्तिन्⟫ m.: the one characterized by a special hand = the elephant (its hand is not an ordinary hand, but a trunk)

::: media
![](/images/lekt3806.webp)
Fig.: ⟪हस्ती⟫
(Image source: [Details](/en/licenses#lekt3806))
:::
⟪हस्तवन्त्⟫ : one who has (human) hands

::: media
![](/images/lekt3807.webp)
Fig.: ⟪हस्तवान्⟫
(Image source: [Details](/en/licenses#lekt3807))
:::

::: grammar-box
Adjectives ending in **-⟪इन्⟫** are frequently used to form compounds.
:::
Example:

⟪सत्यवादिन्⟫ from ⟪सत्यवाद⟫ m. "speaking the truth": "one characterized by speaking the truth = one who always speaks the truth"

## 38.5. Syntax regarding ⟪नामन्⟫
740d0ea002bf73fc47fe34931d7e081a:
::: grammar-box
To express "someone named N. N.", one constructs:

**N.N. (in the nominative) ⟪नाम⟫**

Literally: "the name is/was N.N." Thus, it is an inserted nominal sentence.
:::
Example:

::: indent
⟪आसीद्राजा⟫ ⟪नलो⟫ ⟪नाम⟫ ⟪वीरसेनसुतो⟫ ⟪बली⟫ ⟪।⟫ "Once upon a time there was a king **named Nala**, the strong son of Vīrasena."
:::
Naturally, the same can be expressed with a ⟪बहुव्रीहि⟫:

::: indent
⟪देवदत्तनामा⟫ ⟪पुरुषः⟫ "a man whose name is Devadatta"

⟪मदयन्तिकानाम्नी⟫ ⟪बाला⟫ "a girl whose name is Madayantika"
:::

## 38.6. Syntax regarding ⟪आत्मन्⟫

::: grammar-box
**⟪आत्मन्⟫** **masculine** can be used in the **singular** as a reflexive pronoun for all three genders, numbers (including dual and plural), and persons.
:::
Examples:

::: indent
⟪आत्मन्येषा⟫ ⟪दोषं⟫ ⟪न⟫ ⟪पश्यति⟫ ⟪।⟫ "She sees no fault in herself"

⟪आत्मानं⟫ ⟪स्तुवन्ति⟫ ⟪।⟫ "They praise themselves"
:::
::: grammar-box
The genitive (⟪षष्ठी⟫) **⟪आत्मनस्⟫** can therefore stand for "my/your/his/... own"
:::
Example:

::: indent
⟪आत्मनो⟫ ⟪गृहं⟫ ⟪प्रविशति⟫ ⟪।⟫ "He enters his own house."
:::
## 38.7. Consonant-ending stems as the first member of compounds

::: grammar-box
Stems ending in a consonant appear as the first member of a compound in the (weak) stem they take before the ending -su of the locative (⟪सप्तमी⟫) plural.
:::
Example:

::: indent
***⟪राज⟫***⟪पुत्र⟫ "son of a king"
:::
## 38.8. Stems ending in -an as the second member of a ⟪बहुव्रीहि⟫

::: grammar-box
As the second member of a ⟪बहुव्रीहि⟫, a stem ending in -an can be used for all three genders. However, the feminine is usually formed with the suffix -ī from the weakest masculine stem.
:::
Example:

::: indent
⟪दुर्णाम्नी⟫ "one whose name is evil ; female demon of disease"
:::

# Lesson 28

## 28.1. The Causative (⟪णि⟫, ⟪णिच्⟫, ⟪कारित⟫)

::: grammar-box
**If one wishes to express that someone or something causes or brings about that someone else or something else does or suffers something expressed by a root (with or without a prefix), the causative (⟪णि⟫, ⟪णिच्⟫, ⟪कारित⟫) is used.**

Example:
⟪गम्⟩ "to go" » Causative: ⟪गमयति⟩ "he causes someone to go; he sends"
⟪दृश्⟩ "to see" » Causative: ⟪दर्शयति⟩ "he causes to see = he shows"
:::

## 28.2. Sentence Construction with the Causative (⟪णि⟫, ⟪णिच्⟫, ⟪कारित⟫)

::: grammar-box
**Scheme 1:**

**If the root underlying the causative (with or without a prefix) is INTRANSITIVE (i.e., cannot take an accusative object) or expresses movement, knowledge, information, or eating:**

**Agent (⟪कर्ता⟩) of the causative in the Nominative (⟪प्रथमा⟩) — Agent of the caused action in the Accusative (⟪द्वितीया⟩) — (Target of movement, object of knowledge, etc. in the Accusative = ⟪द्वितीया⟩) — Verb in the Causative**
:::
Examples:

⟪दुर्जनो⟩ ⟪रामं⟩ ⟪मोहयति⟩ = "an evil person causes Rāma to be confused = confuses Rāma = causes Rāma to err"
Result: ⟪रामो⟩ ⟪मुह्यति⟩ = "Rāma is confused / deluded / errs."

⟪रामः⟩ ⟪शत्रून्स्वर्गं⟩ ⟪गमयति⟩ = "Rāma causes the enemies to go to heaven = sends the enemies to heaven"
Result: ⟪शत्रवः⟩ ⟪स्वर्गं⟩ ⟪गच्छन्ति⟩ = "the enemies go to heaven / come to heaven"

⟪गुरू⟩ ⟪रामं⟩ ⟪वेदार्थं⟩ ⟪वेदयति⟩ = "The teacher causes Rāma to know the meaning of the Veda = explains / teaches Rāma the meaning of the Veda"
Result: ⟪रामो⟩ ⟪वेदार्थं⟩ ⟪वेत्ति⟩ = "Rāma knows / understands the meaning of the Veda"

⟪स⟩ ⟪रामं⟩ ⟪वेदमध्यापयति⟩ = "he teaches Rāma the Veda"
Result: ⟪रामो⟩ ⟪वेदमधीते⟩ "Rāma studies the Veda"

⟪रामो⟩ ⟪देवानामृतमाशयति⟩ = "Rāma causes the gods to eat nectar = gives the gods nectar to eat" (⟪अश्⟩ 9 "to eat")
Result: ⟪देवा⟩ ⟪अमृतमश्नन्ति⟩ "The gods eat nectar"

![](/images/lekt2802.webp)
Fig.: ⟪स⟩ ⟪नरान्प्रबन्धविज्ञानमध्यापयति⟩
ISKCON Temple Bangalore.
(Image source: [Details](/en/licenses#lekt2801))
:::

::: grammar-box
**Also constructed according to Scheme 1 is the root ⟪दृश्⟩:**

**Exceptions to Scheme 1 see under Scheme 2**

Example:
(⟪स⟩) ⟪रामं⟩ ⟪पुत्रं⟩ ⟪दर्शयति⟩ = "he shows the son to Rāma"
:::
The following verse summarizes examples of causative formation according to Scheme 1 (the verbal forms are each the 3rd Person Imperfect Parasmaipada):
::: indent
⟪शत्रूनगमयत्स्वर्गं⟫
⟪वेदार्थं⟫ ⟪स्वानवेदयत्⟫ ⟪।⟫
⟪आशयच्चामृतं⟫ ⟪देवान्⟫
⟪वेदमध्यापयद्विधिम्⟫ ⟪।⟫
⟪आसयत्सलिलै⟫ ⟪पृथ्वीं⟫
⟪यः⟫ ⟪स⟫ ⟪मे⟫ ⟪श्रीहरिगतिः⟫ ⟪॥⟫
:::

::: indent
My refuge and my goal is Hari,
Who sent the enemies to heaven,
Who taught his followers the meaning of the Veda,
Who fed the gods with nectar,
Who taught the Creator the Veda,
Who set the earth in the water.
:::

::: grammar-box
**Schema 2:**

**With transitive verbs (except those mentioned under Schema 1). Also with all verbs, when the action designated by the causative is caused (i.e., when the causative is a causative of a causative):**
4cca88dd1bbade5c0f4d93aacf713c86:
**Agent (⟪कर्ता⟫) of the causative in the Nominative (⟪प्रथमा⟫) — Agent of the caused action in the Instrumental (⟪तृतीया⟫) — Object of the caused action in the case it would have according to the simple verb (i.e., usually in the Accusative) — Verb in the causative**
:::
::: indent
Examples:
(⟪स⟫) ⟪रामेण⟫ ⟪भार्यां⟫ ⟪त्याजयति⟫ = "He causes Rāma to leave his wife"
Result: ⟪रामो⟫ ⟪भार्यां⟫ ⟪त्यजति⟫ = "Rāma leaves his wife"

⟪विष्णुमित्रो⟫ ⟪रामेण⟫ ⟪गोविन्दं⟫ ⟪गमयति⟫ = "Viṣṇumitra causes Rāma to cause Govinda to go = Viṣṇumitra has Rāma send Govinda away"
Result: ⟪रामो⟫ ⟪गोविन्दं⟫ ⟪गमयति⟫ = "Rāma sends Govinda away"
Result of this result: ⟪गोविन्दो⟫ ⟪गच्छति⟫ = "Govinda goes"
:::
::: grammar-box
**Exceptions to Schema 1:**

**The following verbs also construct according to Schema 2:**

**Causative of:**
- **⟪नी⟫ "to lead"**
- **⟪वह्⟫ "to travel" (only when the agent of the caused action is not the driver)**
- **⟪स्मृ⟫ "to recall" (there are exceptions to this)**
- **⟪अद्⟫ "to eat"**
- **⟪खाद्⟫ "to chew"**
:::
Examples:

⟪रामो⟫ ⟪भृत्येन⟫ ⟪भारं⟫ ⟪नाययति⟫ ⟪वाहयति⟫ ⟪वा⟫ = "Rāma has the servant lead or travel with the burden"
Result: ⟪भृत्यो⟫ ⟪भारं⟫ ⟪नयति⟫ ⟪वहति⟫ ⟪वा⟫ = "The servant leads or travels with the burden"

⟪रामो⟫ ⟪बालेनान्नमादयति⟫ ⟪खादयति⟫ ⟪वा⟫ = "Rāma has the boy eat or chew food"
Result: ⟪बालो⟫ ⟪ऽन्नमत्ति⟫ ⟪खादति⟫ ⟪वा⟫ = "the boy eats or chews food"

(⟪स⟫) ⟪रामेण⟫ ⟪स्मारयति⟫ = "He causes Rāma to remember"
Result: ⟪रामः⟫ ⟪स्मरति⟫ = "Rāma remembers"

::: grammar-box
**The following causatives can construct both according to Schema 1 and according to Schema 2:**

- **⟪हृ⟫ "to hold, to fetch"**
- **⟪कृ⟫ "to do, to make"**
- **Ātmanepadakausative of ⟪दृश्⟫**
:::
Examples:

⟪रामो⟫ ⟪भृत्यं⟫ ⟪कटं⟫ ⟪कारयति⟫ ⟪हारयति⟫ ⟪वा⟫ = "Rāma has the servant make or fetch a mat (⟪कट⟫ f.)"
or:
⟪रामो⟫ ⟪भृत्येन⟫ ⟪कटं⟫ ⟪कारयति⟫ ⟪हारयति⟫ ⟪वा⟫
Result: ⟪भृत्यः⟫ ⟪कटं⟫ ⟪करोति⟫ ⟪हरति⟫ ⟪वा⟫ = "The servant makes or fetches a mat"

⟪रामो⟫ ⟪बालं⟫ ⟪प्रतिमां⟫ ⟪दर्शयते⟫ = "Rāma has the boy see the image = shows the boy the image (for his own interest)"
or:
⟪रामो⟫ ⟪बालेन⟫ ⟪प्रतिमां⟫ ⟪दर्शयते⟫
Result: ⟪बालः⟫ ⟪प्रतिमां⟫ ⟪पश्यति⟫ = "the boy sees the image"

When the causative is used in a passive construction, the following schema is almost always applied:

::: grammar-box
**Schema A (Passive construction):**

**Agent of the causative in the Instrumental (⟪तृतीया⟫) — Agent of the caused action in the Nominative (⟪प्रथमा⟫) — Object of the caused action in the case it would have according to the simple verb (i.e., usually in the Accusative) — Verb in the causative**
:::
Examples:

⟪गुरुणा⟫ ⟪रामो⟫ ⟪ग्रामं⟫ ⟪गम्यते⟫ = "The master sends Rāma to the village"
Result: ⟪रामो⟫ ⟪ग्रामं⟫ ⟪गच्छति⟫ = "Rāma goes to the village"

⟪रामेण⟫ ⟪भृत्यः⟫ ⟪कटं⟫ ⟪कार्यते⟫ = "Rāma has the servant make a mat"
Result: ⟪भृत्यः⟫ ⟪कटं⟫ ⟪करोति⟫ = "The servant makes a mat"

⟪रामेण⟫ ⟪भृत्यो⟫ ⟪भारं⟫ ⟪हार्यते⟫ = "Rāma has the servant fetch the load"
Result: ⟪भृत्यो⟫ ⟪भारं⟫ ⟪हरति⟫ = "The servant fetches the load"

## 28.3. Formation of the present stem from the causative (⟪णि⟫, ⟪णिच्⟫, ⟪कारित⟫)
99c563e99572259f4d8050db9132e758:
::: grammar-box
**The thematic endings of the present stem are added to the causative stem**
:::
There are various formation types:

::: grammar-box
**Formation type 1: (usually) guṇa-grade root + -aya-**
:::
Examples:

| Root | Kausativ 3. sg. Indikativ Present | Meaning |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| ⟪विश्⟫ | ⟪वेशयति⟫ | he/she/it causes to enter, leads in |
| ⟪लुभ्⟫ | ⟪लोभयति⟫ | cause to desire, make desirous, entice |
| ⟪दृश्⟫ | ⟪दर्शयति⟫ | cause to see = show |
| ⟪वृत्⟫ | ⟪वर्तयति⟫ | cause to turn, turn (transitive), roll (transitive), set in motion |

::: grammar-box
**Formation type 2: dīrgha-grade root + -aya-**

**Often with roots ending in a vowel, and with roots where a single final consonant follows -a-.**
:::
Examples:

| Root | Kausativ 3. sg. Indikativ Present | Meaning |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| ⟪भू⟫ | ⟪भावयति⟫:br(aus: bhau-aya-ti) | cause someone or something to become, produce |
| ⟪इ⟫ | ⟪आययति⟫:br(aus: ai-aya-ti) | cause someone to go |
| ⟪नी⟫ | ⟪नाययति⟫:br(aus: nai-aya-ti) | cause to lead |
| ⟪कृ⟫ | ⟪कारयति⟫:br(kār-aya-ti) | cause to do |

::: grammar-box
**Formation type 3: zero-grade root + -aya-**

**Occurs.**
:::
Example:

| Root | Kausativ 3. sg. Indikativ Present | Meaning |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| ⟪दुष्⟫ | ⟪दूषयति⟫:br(dūṣ-aya-ti) | (to) corrupt |

::: grammar-box
**Formation type 4: root + -paya-**

**With roots ending in -ā and some other roots.**
:::
Examples:

| Root | Kausativ 3. sg. Indikativ Present | Meaning |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| ⟪स्था⟫ | ⟪स्थापयति⟫:br(sthā-paya-ti) | cause to stand, set up |
| ⟪इ⟫ + ⟪अधि⟫:br"studieren" | ⟪अध्यापयति⟫:br(aus: adhi+ā-paya-ti):br(zur Explanation siehe Thumb-Hauschildt Bd. I,2 S. 341) | cause to study, instruct |

::: grammar-box
**Irregular formations:**

**Native grammarians consider the following forms as causatives:**

- **han** : Caus. **ghātayati**¹ "cause to strike, cause to kill"
- **pā** 2 "to protect": **pālayati**² "to bring across, save, protect"
:::
Notes:
1. **ghātayati** is in reality a verb derived from the noun **ghāta** m. "blow" (denominative) and is used instead of the causative of **han**.
2. **pālayati** is a genuine causative, but from the root **pṛ** 3 "to bring across, save, protect": **pārayati** (pār-aya-ti) » **pālayati** (in some parts of India r corresponds to l, in others conversely l corresponds to r).

## 28.4. Formation of the Passive (⟪यक्⟫) from the Causative

::: grammar-box
**The passive of the causative is formed as follows:**

**Causative stem WITHOUT -aya- + passive suffix -ya-**

Examples:
**bhāvyate** (bhāv-ya-te) "he/she/it is brought forth"
**sthāpyate** (sthāp-ya-te) "he/she/it is placed"
:::
While the passive of the original root is usually formed from the guṇa-grade root, the passive of the causative can usually be recognized by the fact that it is formed from the strong or lengthened-grade root.

## 28.5. Formation of the Future (⟪ऌट्⟫, ⟪भविष्यन्ती⟫ f.) from the Causative
01b7dac68dddabd5244b9d9e00eecddf:
::: grammar-box
**The future of the causative is formed from the causative stem, whereby the final -a- of the causative suffix is dropped:**

**-ay-iṣya-**

Example:
**budh** Future-Causative: **bodhayiṣyati** (bodh-ay-i-ṣya-ti): "he/she/it will awaken"
:::

## 28.6. Formation of the PPP (⟪क्त⟫) from the Causative

::: grammar-box
**Causative stem on -ay- (without final a) + -i- + -ta**

Examples:
**gam** — **gamayati** — **gamita** (gam-i-ta) "sent" (PPP of the simple root: **gata**)
**sthā** — **sthāpayati** — **sthāpita** (sthāp-i-ta) "placed"
:::

## 28.7. Formation of the Absolutives (⟪क्त्वा⟫ . ⟪ल्यप्⟫) from the Causative

::: grammar-box
**The -tvā absolute is formed from the causative stem on -ay- (without final a):**

**Causative stem on -ay- + -i- + -tvā**

Example:
**sthāpayitvā** (sthā-pay-i-tvā) "after having placed"
:::
::: grammar-box
**The -ya absolute occurs with causatives having a prefix usually on the causative stem WITHOUT -aya-**

Examples:
**prabudh** — **prabodhayati** — **prabodhya** (pra-bodh-ya) "after having awakened"
**ānī** — **ānayati** — **ānāyya** (ā-nāy-ya) "after having caused to bring near, after having caused to bring"
:::
::: grammar-box
**However, if the root syllable of the causative contains a short -a- before a single consonant, the -ya of the absolute attaches to the causative stem on -ay- (without final a)**

Example:
**āgam** — **āgamayati** — **āgamayya** (ā-gamay-ya) "after having caused to come"
:::

## 28.8. Formation of the Infinitive (⟪तुमुन्⟫) from the Causative

::: grammar-box
**The infinitive of the causative is formed from the causative stem on -ay- (without final a):**

**Causative stem on -ay- + -i- + -tum**

Example:
**jan** — **janayati** — **janayitum** (janay-i-tum) "in order to produce"
:::

## 28.9. The 10th Present Class (⟪चुरादि⟫ = ⟪चुर्⟫ etc.)

::: grammar-box
**In the same way as causatives, some roots of the 10th present class form the present (and the other tenses) without being causatives.**

Examples:
1.  Lengthened-grade root + -aya- : ⟪कम्⟫ 10Ā ⟪कामयते⟫ "to love"
2.  Strong-grade root + -aya- : **cur** 10U **corayati** "to steal"; Future: **corayiṣyate**; Passive: **coryate**
:::
::: grammar-box
**The forms of the causative of verbs of the 10th present class are identical with the forms of the simple verb. The decision as to whether a causative is present is possible only from the meaning or sometimes from the construction.**
:::
